in &#39;fraud&#39;">ɔː</span><span title="&#39;l&#39; in &#39;lie&#39;">l</span></span>-/</a></span>&#32;<span data-nosnippet="" id="ooui-php-1" class="ext-phonos ext-phonos-PhonosButton noexcerpt ext-phonos-PhonosButton-emptylabel oo-ui-widget oo-ui-widget-enabled oo-ui-buttonElement oo-ui-buttonElement-frameless oo-ui-iconElement oo-ui-buttonWidget" data-ooui="{&quot;_&quot;:&quot;mw.Phonos.PhonosButton&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;\/\/upload.wikimedia.org\/wikipedia\/commons\/transcoded\/b\/b3\/En-us-Albania.ogg\/En-us-Albania.ogg.mp3&quot;,&quot;rel&quot;:[&quot;nofollow&quot;],&quot;framed&quot;:false,&quot;icon&quot;:&quot;volumeUp&quot;,&quot;data&quot;:{&quot;ipa&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;text&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;lang&quot;:&quot;en&quot;,&quot;wikibase&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;file&quot;:&quot;En-us-Albania.ogg&quot;},&quot;classes&quot;:[&quot;ext-phonos&quot;,&quot;ext-phonos-PhonosButton&quot;,&quot;noexcerpt&quot;,&quot;ext-phonos-PhonosButton-emptylabel&quot;]}"><a role="button" tabindex="0" href="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/b/b3/En-us-Albania.ogg/En-us-Albania.ogg.mp3" rel="nofollow" aria-label="Play audio" class="oo-ui-buttonElement-button"><span class="oo-ui-iconElement-icon oo-ui-icon-volumeUp"></span><span class="oo-ui-labelElement-label"></span><span class="oo-ui-indicatorElement-indicator oo-ui-indicatorElement-noIndicator"></span></a></span><sup class="ext-phonos-attribution noexcerpt"><a href="/wiki/File:En-us-Albania.ogg" title="File:En-us-Albania.ogg">i</a></sup></span> <a href="/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key" title="Help:Pronunciation respelling key"><i title="English pronunciation respelling">a(w)l-<span style="font-size:90%">BAY</span>-nee-ə</i></a>; <a href="/wiki/Albanian_language" title="Albanian language">Albanian</a>: <i lang="sq">Shqipëri</i> or <span title="Albanian-language text"><i lang="sq">Shqipëria</i></span>),<sup id="cite_ref-8" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-8">&#91;a&#93;</a></sup> officially the <b>Republic of Albania</b> (Albanian: <i lang="sq">Republika e Shqipërisë</i>),<sup id="cite_ref-9" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-9">&#91;b&#93;</a></sup> is a country in <a href="/wiki/Southeast_Europe" title="Southeast Europe">Southeast Europe</a>. The country is located in the <a href="/wiki/Balkans" title="Balkans">Balkans</a> on the <a href="/wiki/Adriatic_Sea" title="Adriatic Sea">Adriatic</a> and <a href="/wiki/Ionian_Sea" title="Ionian Sea">Ionian Seas</a> within the <a href="/wiki/Mediterranean_Sea" title="Mediterranean Sea">Mediterranean Sea</a> and shares <a href="/wiki/Land_border" class="mw-redirect" title="Land border">land borders</a> with <a href="/wiki/Montenegro" title="Montenegro">Montenegro</a> to the northwest, <a href="/wiki/Kosovo" title="Kosovo">Kosovo</a> to the northeast, <a href="/wiki/North_Macedonia" title="North Macedonia">North Macedonia</a> to the east and <a href="/wiki/Greece" title="Greece">Greece</a> to the south. Spanning an area of 28,748&#160;km<sup>2</sup> (11,100&#160;sq&#160;mi), it displays a varied range of climatic, geological, hydrological and morphological conditions. The country's landscapes range from rugged snow-capped mountains in the <a href="/wiki/Accursed_Mountains" title="Accursed Mountains">Albanian Alps</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Korab" title="Korab">Korab</a>, <a href="/wiki/Central_Mountain_Range,_Albania#Skanderbeg_Mountains" class="mw-redirect" title="Central Mountain Range, Albania">Skanderbeg</a>, <a href="/wiki/Pindus" title="Pindus">Pindus</a> and <a href="/wiki/Ceraunian_Mountains" title="Ceraunian Mountains">Ceraunian Mountains</a>, to fertile lowland plains extending from the coasts of the <a href="/wiki/Albanian_Adriatic_Sea_Coast" title="Albanian Adriatic Sea Coast">Adriatic</a> and <a href="/wiki/Albanian_Ionian_Sea_Coast" title="Albanian Ionian Sea Coast">Ionian</a> seas. <a href="/wiki/Tirana" title="Tirana">Tirana</a> is the capital and largest city in the country, followed by <a href="/wiki/Durr%C3%ABs" title="Durrës">Durrës</a>, <a href="/wiki/Vlor%C3%AB" title="Vlorë">Vlorë</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Shkod%C3%ABr" title="Shkodër">Shkodër</a>.
</p><p>In ancient times, the <a href="/wiki/Illyrians" title="Illyrians">Illyrians</a> inhabited northern and central regions of Albania, whilst <a href="/wiki/Epirotes" class="mw-redirect" title="Epirotes">Epirotes</a> inhabited the south. Several important ancient <a href="/wiki/Greek_colonisation" title="Greek colonisation">Greek colonies</a> were also established on the coast. In the 2nd century BCE, the region was annexed by the <a href="/wiki/Roman_Republic" title="Roman Republic">Roman Republic</a>, and after the division of the <a href="/wiki/Roman_Empire" title="Roman Empire">Roman Empire</a> it became part of <a href="/wiki/Byzantine_Empire" title="Byzantine Empire">Byzantium</a>. The first known <a href="/wiki/Albanians" title="Albanians">Albanian</a> autonomous principality – <a href="/wiki/Arbanon" class="mw-redirect" title="Arbanon">Arbanon</a> – was established in the 12th century. The <a href="/wiki/Kingdom_of_Albania_(medieval)" title="Kingdom of Albania (medieval)">Kingdom of Albania</a>, <a href="/wiki/Principality_of_Albania_(medieval)" title="Principality of Albania (medieval)">Principality of Albania</a> and <a href="/wiki/Albania_Veneta" class="mw-redirect" title="Albania Veneta">Albania Veneta</a> were formed between the 13th and 15th centuries in different parts of the country, alongside other Albanian principalities and political entities. In the late 15th century, Albania <a href="/wiki/Ottoman_Albania" class="mw-redirect" title="Ottoman Albania">became part</a> of the <a href="/wiki/Ottoman_Empire" title="Ottoman Empire">Ottoman Empire</a> until 1912, when the modern Albanian state <a href="/wiki/Declaration_of_independence_of_Albania" class="mw-redirect" title="Declaration of independence of Albania">declared independence</a>. In 1939, the <a href="/wiki/Kingdom_of_Albania_(1928%E2%80%9339)" class="mw-redirect" title="Kingdom of Albania (1928–39)">Kingdom of Albania</a> was invaded by <a href="/wiki/Kingdom_of_Italy" title="Kingdom of Italy">Italy</a>, which became <a href="/wiki/Albanian_Kingdom_(1939%E2%80%9343)" class="mw-redirect" title="Albanian Kingdom (1939–43)">Greater Albania</a>, and then a <a href="/wiki/Albanian_Kingdom_(1943%E2%80%9344)" class="mw-redirect" title="Albanian Kingdom (1943–44)">protectorate</a> of <a href="/wiki/Nazi_Germany" title="Nazi Germany">Nazi Germany</a> during <a href="/wiki/World_War_II" title="World War II">World War II</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-zolo2002_10-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-zolo2002-10">&#91;8&#93;</a></sup> Following the war, the <a href="/wiki/People%27s_Socialist_Republic_of_Albania" title="People&#39;s Socialist Republic of Albania">People's Socialist Republic of Albania</a> was formed, which lasted until the <a href="/wiki/Revolutions_of_1989" title="Revolutions of 1989">Revolutions of 1991</a> concluded with the <a href="/wiki/Fall_of_communism_in_Albania" title="Fall of communism in Albania">fall of communism in Albania</a> and eventually the establishment of the current Republic of Albania.
</p><p>Albania is a <a href="/wiki/Unitary_state" title="Unitary state">unitary</a> <a href="/wiki/Parliamentary_system" title="Parliamentary system">parliamentary</a> <a href="/wiki/Constitutional_republic" class="mw-redirect" title="Constitutional republic">constitutional republic</a>. It is a <a href="/wiki/Developing_country" title="Developing country">developing country</a>, ranking 67th in the <a href="/wiki/Human_Development_Index" title="Human Development Index">Human Development Index</a>, with an upper-middle income <a href="/wiki/Economy_of_Albania" title="Economy of Albania">economy</a> dominated by the service sector, followed by manufacturing.<sup id="cite_ref-11" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-11">&#91;9&#93;</a></sup> It went through a process of transition following the end of communism in 1990, from centralised planning to a <a href="/wiki/Market-based_economy" class="mw-redirect" title="Market-based economy">market-based economy</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-12" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-12">&#91;10&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-13" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-13">&#91;11&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-14" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-14">&#91;12&#93;</a></sup> Albania provides <a href="/wiki/Healthcare_in_Albania" title="Healthcare in Albania">universal health care</a> and free primary and secondary <a href="/wiki/Education_in_Albania" title="Education in Albania">education</a> to its citizens.<sup id="cite_ref-HDI_6-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-HDI-6">&#91;6&#93;</a></sup> Albania is a member of the United Nations, <a href="/wiki/World_Bank" title="World Bank">World Bank</a>, <a href="/wiki/UNESCO" title="UNESCO">UNESCO</a>, <a href="/wiki/NATO" title="NATO">NATO</a>, <a href="/wiki/World_Trade_Organization" title="World Trade Organization">WTO</a>, <a href="/wiki/Council_of_Europe" title="Council of Europe">COE</a>, <a href="/wiki/Organization_for_Security_and_Co-operation_in_Europe" title="Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe">OSCE</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Organisation_of_Islamic_Cooperation" title="Organisation of Islamic Cooperation">OIC</a>. It has been an <a href="/wiki/Accession_of_Albania_to_the_European_Union" title="Accession of Albania to the European Union">official candidate</a> for membership in the <a href="/wiki/European_Union" title="European Union">European Union</a> since 2014. It is one of the founding members of the <a href="/wiki/Energy_Community" title="Energy Community">Energy Community</a>, including the <a href="/wiki/Organization_of_the_Black_Sea_Economic_Cooperation" title="Organization of the Black Sea Economic Cooperation">Organization of the Black Sea Economic Cooperation</a> and <a href="/wiki/Union_for_the_Mediterranean" title="Union for the Mediterranean">Union for the Mediterranean</a>.
</p>
<style data-mw-deduplicate="TemplateStyles:r886046785">.mw-parser-output .toclimit-2 .toclevel-1 ul,.mw-parser-output .toclimit-3 .toclevel-2 ul,.mw-parser-output .toclimit-4 .toclevel-3 ul,.mw-parser-output .toclimit-5 .toclevel-4 ul,.mw-parser-output .toclimit-6 .toclevel-5 ul,.mw-parser-output .toclimit-7 .toclevel-6 ul{display:none}</style><div class="toclimit-3"><meta property="mw:PageProp/toc" /></div>
<p><span class="anchor" id="Etymology"></span><span class="anchor" id="Toponymy"></span><span class="anchor" id="Names"></span>
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Name">Name</span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Names_of_the_Albanians_and_Albania" title="Names of the Albanians and Albania">Names of the Albanians and Albania</a></div>
<p>The historical origins of the term "Albania" can be traced back to <a href="/wiki/Medieval_Latin" title="Medieval Latin">medieval Latin</a>, with its foundations believed to be associated with the <a href="/wiki/Illyrian_tribe" class="mw-redirect" title="Illyrian tribe">Illyrian tribe</a> of the <a href="/wiki/Albani_(Illyrian_tribe)" class="mw-redirect" title="Albani (Illyrian tribe)">Albani</a>. This connection gains further support from the work of the Ancient Greek geographer Ptolemy during the 2nd century AD, where he included the settlement of <a href="/wiki/Albanopolis" title="Albanopolis">Albanopolis</a> situated to the northeast of <a href="/wiki/Durr%C3%ABs" title="Durrës">Durrës</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-15" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-15">&#91;13&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-16" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-16">&#91;14&#93;</a></sup> The presence of a medieval settlement named <a href="/wiki/Principality_of_Arbanon" title="Principality of Arbanon">Albanon</a> or Arbanon hints at the possibility of historical continuity. However, the precise relationship between these historical references and the question of whether Albanopolis was synonymous with Albanon remains a subject of scholarly debate.<sup id="cite_ref-17" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-17">&#91;15&#93;</a></sup> The Byzantine historian <a href="/wiki/Michael_Attaliates" class="mw-redirect" title="Michael Attaliates">Michael Attaliates</a>, in his 11th century historical account, provides the earliest undisputed reference to the Albanians, when he mentions them having taken part in a revolt against <a href="/wiki/Constantinople" title="Constantinople">Constantinople</a> in 1079.<sup id="cite_ref-MadgearuGordon25b_18-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-MadgearuGordon25b-18">&#91;16&#93;</a></sup> Additionally, he identified the Arbanitai as subjects under the governance of the Duke of <a href="/wiki/Durr%C3%ABs" title="Durrës">Dyrrachium</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-19" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-19">&#91;17&#93;</a></sup> In the Middle Ages, Albania was denoted as <span title="Albanian-language text"><i lang="sq">Arbëri</i></span> or <span title="Albanian-language text"><i lang="sq">Arbëni</i></span> by its inhabitants, who identified themselves as <span title="Albanian-language text"><i lang="sq">Arbëreshë</i></span> or <span title="Albanian-language text"><i lang="sq">Arbëneshë</i></span>.<sup id="cite_ref-20" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-20">&#91;18&#93;</a></sup> Presently, Albanians employs the terms <span title="Albanian-language text"><i lang="sq">Shqipëri</i></span> or <span title="Albanian-language text"><i lang="sq">Shqipëria</i></span> when referring to their nation, designations  that trace their historical origins to the 14th century.<sup id="cite_ref-Matasović_21-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Matasović-21">&#91;19&#93;</a></sup> However, it was not until the late 17th and early 18th centuries that these terms gradually superseded <span title="Albanian-language text"><i lang="sq">Arbëria</i></span> and <span title="Albanian-language text"><i lang="sq">Arbëreshë</i></span> among the Albanians.<sup id="cite_ref-Matasović_21-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Matasović-21">&#91;19&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Lloshi_22-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Lloshi-22">&#91;20&#93;</a></sup> These two expressions are widely interpreted to symbolise "Children of the Eagles" and "Land of the Eagles".<sup id="cite_ref-23" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-23">&#91;21&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-24" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-24">&#91;22&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="History">History</span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">For a chronological guide, see <a href="/wiki/Timeline_of_Albanian_history" title="Timeline of Albanian history">Timeline of Albanian history</a>.</div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/History_of_Albania" title="History of Albania">History of Albania</a></div>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Prehistory">Prehistory</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Prehistoric_Albania" title="Prehistoric Albania">Prehistory of Albania</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Kamenic%C3%AB_Tumulus,_Albania_2018_02.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a7/Kamenic%C3%AB_Tumulus%2C_Albania_2018_02.jpg/220px-Kamenic%C3%AB_Tumulus%2C_Albania_2018_02.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="146" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a7/Kamenic%C3%AB_Tumulus%2C_Albania_2018_02.jpg/330px-Kamenic%C3%AB_Tumulus%2C_Albania_2018_02.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a7/Kamenic%C3%AB_Tumulus%2C_Albania_2018_02.jpg/440px-Kamenic%C3%AB_Tumulus%2C_Albania_2018_02.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1800" data-file-height="1192" /></a><figcaption>The remains of the <a href="/wiki/Kamenica_Tumulus" title="Kamenica Tumulus">Kamenica Tumulus</a> in the <a href="/wiki/County_of_Kor%C3%A7%C3%AB" class="mw-redirect" title="County of Korçë">county of Korçë</a>.</figcaption></figure>
<p>Mesolithic habitation in Albania has been evidenced in several open air sites which during that period were close to the Adriatic coastline and in cave sites. Mesolithic objects found in a cave near Xarrë include <a href="/wiki/Flint" title="Flint">flint</a> and <a href="/wiki/Jasper" title="Jasper">jasper</a> objects along with fossilised animal bones, while those discoveries at Mount Dajt comprise bone and stone tools similar to those of the <a href="/wiki/Aurignacian_culture" class="mw-redirect" title="Aurignacian culture">Aurignacian culture</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Prendi_25-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Prendi-25">&#91;23&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Neolithic" title="Neolithic">Neolithic</a> era in Albania began around 7000 BCE and is evidenced in finds which indicate domestication of sheep and goats and small-scale agriculture. A part of the Neolithic population may have been the same as the Mesolithic population of the southern Balkans like in the <a href="/wiki/Konispol" title="Konispol">Konispol</a> cave where the Mesolithic stratum co-exists with Pre-Pottery Neolithic finds. <a href="/wiki/Cardium_pottery" title="Cardium pottery">Cardium pottery</a> culture appears in coastal Albania and across the Adriatic after 6500 BCE, while the settlements of the interior took part in the processes which formed <a href="/wiki/Star%C4%8Devo_culture" title="Starčevo culture">Starčevo culture</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-26" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-26">&#91;24&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/Indo-European_migrations" title="Indo-European migrations">Indo-Europeanization</a> of Albania in the context of the IE-ization of the western Balkans began after 2800 BCE. The presence of the Early Bronze Age <a href="/wiki/Tumulus" title="Tumulus">tumuli</a> in the vicinity of later <a href="/wiki/Apollonia_(Illyria)" title="Apollonia (Illyria)">Apollonia</a> dates to  2679±174 calBCE (2852-2505 calBCE). These burial mounds belong to the southern expression of the Adriatic-Ljubljana culture (related to later <a href="/wiki/Cetina_culture" title="Cetina culture">Cetina culture</a>) which moved southwards along the Adriatic from the northern Balkans. The same community built similar mounds in Montenegro (Rakića Kuće) and northern Albania (Shtoj).<sup id="cite_ref-27" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-27">&#91;25&#93;</a></sup> The first archaeogenetic find related to the IE-ization of Albania involves a man with predominantly <a href="/wiki/Western_Steppe_Herders" title="Western Steppe Herders">Yamnaya ancestry</a> buried in a tumulus of northeastern Albania which dates to 2663–2472 calBCE.<sup id="cite_ref-28" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-28">&#91;26&#93;</a></sup> During the Middle Bronze Age, Cetina culture sites and finds appear in Albania. Cetina culture moved southwards across the Adriatic from the <a href="/wiki/Cetina" title="Cetina">Cetina valley</a> of <a href="/wiki/Dalmatia" title="Dalmatia">Dalmatia</a>. In Albania, Cetina finds are concentrated around southern <a href="/wiki/Lake_Shkod%C3%ABr" class="mw-redirect" title="Lake Shkodër">Lake Shkodër</a> and appear typically in tumulus cemeteries like in Shkrel and Shtoj and hillforts like Gajtan (Shkodër) as well as cave sites like Blaz, Nezir and Keputa (central Albania) and lake basin sites like Sovjan (southeastern Albania).<sup id="cite_ref-29" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-29">&#91;27&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Antiquity">Antiquity</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/History_of_Albania#Antiquity" title="History of Albania">Antiquity in Albania</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:The_City_and_the_Prokletije_from_the_castle.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f8/The_City_and_the_Prokletije_from_the_castle.jpg/220px-The_City_and_the_Prokletije_from_the_castle.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="121" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f8/The_City_and_the_Prokletije_from_the_castle.jpg/330px-The_City_and_the_Prokletije_from_the_castle.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f8/The_City_and_the_Prokletije_from_the_castle.jpg/440px-The_City_and_the_Prokletije_from_the_castle.jpg 2x" data-file-width="4592" data-file-height="2520" /></a><figcaption>Founded in the 4th century BC, the city of <a href="/wiki/Scodra" class="mw-redirect" title="Scodra">Scodra</a> was the capital of the <a href="/wiki/Illyrian_kingdom" title="Illyrian kingdom">Illyrian kingdom</a> of <a href="/wiki/Ardiaei" title="Ardiaei">Ardiaei</a> and <a href="/wiki/Labeatae" title="Labeatae">Labeatae</a>.</figcaption></figure>
<p>The incorporated territory of Albania was historically inhabited by <a href="/wiki/Indo-European_people" class="mw-redirect" title="Indo-European people">Indo-European peoples</a>, amongst them numerous <a href="/wiki/Illyrian_tribes" class="mw-redirect" title="Illyrian tribes">Illyrian</a> and <a href="/wiki/Epirus_(ancient_state)" title="Epirus (ancient state)">Epirote</a> tribes. There were also several <a href="/wiki/Greek_colonization" class="mw-redirect" title="Greek colonization">Greek colonies</a>. The territory referred to as <a href="/wiki/Illyria" title="Illyria">Illyria</a> corresponded roughly to the area east of the <a href="/wiki/Adriatic_Sea" title="Adriatic Sea">Adriatic Sea</a> in the <a href="/wiki/Mediterranean_Sea" title="Mediterranean Sea">Mediterranean Sea</a> extending in the south to the mouth of the <a href="/wiki/Vjos%C3%AB" class="mw-redirect" title="Vjosë">Vjosë</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-30" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-30">&#91;28&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-31" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-31">&#91;29&#93;</a></sup> The first account of the Illyrian groups comes from <a href="/wiki/Periplus_of_the_Euxine_Sea" title="Periplus of the Euxine Sea">Periplus of the Euxine Sea</a>, a Greek text written in the 4th century BC.<sup id="cite_ref-wilkes_32-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-wilkes-32">&#91;30&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Bryges" title="Bryges">Bryges</a> were also present in  central Albania, while the south was inhabited by the Epirote <a href="/wiki/Chaonians" title="Chaonians">Chaonians</a>, whose capital was at <a href="/wiki/Phoenice" title="Phoenice">Phoenice</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-wilkes_32-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-wilkes-32">&#91;30&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-33" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-33">&#91;31&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-34" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-34">&#91;32&#93;</a></sup> Other colonies such as <a href="/wiki/Apollonia_(Illyria)" title="Apollonia (Illyria)">Apollonia</a> and <a href="/wiki/Epidamnos" title="Epidamnos">Epidamnos</a> were established by Greek city-states on the coast by the 7th century BC.<sup id="cite_ref-wilkes_32-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-wilkes-32">&#91;30&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-35" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-35">&#91;33&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-36" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-36">&#91;34&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Parku_Arkeologjik_i_Apollonis%C3%AB_04.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/39/Parku_Arkeologjik_i_Apollonis%C3%AB_04.jpg/220px-Parku_Arkeologjik_i_Apollonis%C3%AB_04.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="150" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/39/Parku_Arkeologjik_i_Apollonis%C3%AB_04.jpg/330px-Parku_Arkeologjik_i_Apollonis%C3%AB_04.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/39/Parku_Arkeologjik_i_Apollonis%C3%AB_04.jpg/440px-Parku_Arkeologjik_i_Apollonis%C3%AB_04.jpg 2x" data-file-width="4016" data-file-height="2745" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Apollonia_(Illyria)" title="Apollonia (Illyria)">Apollonia</a> was an important <a href="/wiki/Colonies_in_antiquity#Greek_colonies" title="Colonies in antiquity">Greek colony</a> on the <a href="/wiki/Illyria" title="Illyria">Illyrian</a> coast along the <a href="/wiki/Adriatic_Sea" title="Adriatic Sea">Adriatic Sea</a> and one of the western points of the <a href="/wiki/Via_Egnatia" title="Via Egnatia">Via Egnatia</a> route, that connected Rome and <a href="/wiki/Constantinople" title="Constantinople">Constantinople</a>.</figcaption></figure>
<p>The Illyrian <a href="/wiki/Taulantii" title="Taulantii">Taulanti</a> were a powerful Illyrian tribe that were among the earliest recorded tribes in the area. They lived in a area that corresponds much of present-day Albania. Together with the Dardanian ruler <a href="/wiki/Cleitus_(son_of_Bardylis)" title="Cleitus (son of Bardylis)">Cleitus</a>, <a href="/wiki/Glaucias_of_Taulantii" title="Glaucias of Taulantii">Glaucias</a>, the ruler of the Taulantian kingdom, fought against <a href="/wiki/Alexander_the_Great" title="Alexander the Great">Alexander the Great</a> at the <a href="/wiki/Siege_of_Pelium" title="Siege of Pelium">Battle of Pelium</a> in 335 BC. As the time passed, the ruler of Ancient Macedonia, <a href="/wiki/Cassander" title="Cassander">Cassander of Macedon</a> captured Apollonia and crossed the river <a href="/wiki/Shkumbin" title="Shkumbin">Genusus</a> (<a href="/wiki/Albanian_language" title="Albanian language">Albanian</a>: <i lang="sq">Shkumbin</i>) in 314 BC. A few years later Glaucias laid siege to Apollonia and captured the Greek colony of <a href="/wiki/Epidamnos" title="Epidamnos">Epidamnos</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-37" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-37">&#91;35&#93;</a></sup> 
</p><p>The Illyrian <a href="/wiki/Ardiaei" title="Ardiaei">Ardiaei</a> tribe, centred in Montenegro, ruled over most of the territory of northern Albania. Their <a href="/wiki/Ardiaean_Kingdom" class="mw-redirect" title="Ardiaean Kingdom">Ardiaean Kingdom</a> reached its greatest extent under <a href="/wiki/Agron_of_Illyria" title="Agron of Illyria">King Agron</a>, the son of <a href="/wiki/Pleuratus_II" title="Pleuratus II">Pleuratus II</a>. Agron extended his rule over other neighbouring tribes as well.<sup id="cite_ref-38" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-38">&#91;36&#93;</a></sup> Following Agron's death in 230 BC, his wife, <a href="/wiki/Teuta" title="Teuta">Teuta</a>, inherited the&#160;Ardiaean kingdom. Teuta's forces extended their operations further southwards to the&#160;Ionian Sea.<sup id="cite_ref-39" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-39">&#91;37&#93;</a></sup> In 229 BC, Rome declared war<sup id="cite_ref-40" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-40">&#91;38&#93;</a></sup> on the kingdom for extensively plundering Roman ships. The war ended in Illyrian defeat in 227&#160;BC. Teuta was eventually succeeded by&#160;<a href="/wiki/Gentius" title="Gentius">Gentius</a>&#160;in 181&#160;BC.<sup id="cite_ref-41" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-41">&#91;39&#93;</a></sup> Gentius clashed with the Romans in 168&#160;BC, initiating the <a href="/wiki/Third_Illyrian_War" class="mw-redirect" title="Third Illyrian War">Third Illyrian War</a>. The conflict resulted in Roman conquest of the region by 167&#160;BC. The Romans split the region into three administrative divisions.<sup id="cite_ref-42" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-42">&#91;40&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Middle_Ages">Middle Ages</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Albania_in_the_Middle_Ages" title="Albania in the Middle Ages">Albania in the Middle Ages</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Kruj%C3%AB-KrujaAlbania_2016.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/43/Kruj%C3%AB-KrujaAlbania_2016.jpg/220px-Kruj%C3%AB-KrujaAlbania_2016.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/43/Kruj%C3%AB-KrujaAlbania_2016.jpg/330px-Kruj%C3%AB-KrujaAlbania_2016.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/43/Kruj%C3%AB-KrujaAlbania_2016.jpg/440px-Kruj%C3%AB-KrujaAlbania_2016.jpg 2x" data-file-width="6000" data-file-height="4000" /></a><figcaption>The town of <a href="/wiki/Kruj%C3%AB" title="Krujë">Krujë</a> was the capital of the <a href="/wiki/Principality_of_Arbanon" title="Principality of Arbanon">Principality of Arbanon</a> in the Middle Ages.</figcaption></figure>
<p>The <a href="/wiki/Roman_Empire" title="Roman Empire">Roman Empire</a> was split in 395 upon the death of <a href="/wiki/Theodosius_I" title="Theodosius I">Theodosius I</a> into an <a href="/wiki/Eastern_Roman_Empire" class="mw-redirect" title="Eastern Roman Empire">Eastern</a> and <a href="/wiki/Western_Roman_Empire" title="Western Roman Empire">Western Roman Empire</a> in part because of the increasing pressure from threats during the <a href="/wiki/Barbarian_Invasions" class="mw-redirect" title="Barbarian Invasions">Barbarian Invasions</a>. From the 6th century into the 7th century, the <a href="/wiki/South_Slavs" title="South Slavs">Slavs</a> crossed the <a href="/wiki/Danube" title="Danube">Danube</a> and largely absorbed the indigenous Greeks, Illyrians and Thracians in the <a href="/wiki/Balkans" title="Balkans">Balkans</a>; thus, the Illyrians were mentioned for the last time in historical records in the 7th century.<sup id="cite_ref-BideleuxJeffries2007_43-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-BideleuxJeffries2007-43">&#91;41&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Schaefer2008_44-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Schaefer2008-44">&#91;42&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In the 11th century, the <a href="/wiki/Great_Schism_of_1054" class="mw-redirect" title="Great Schism of 1054">Great Schism</a> formalised the break of communion between the <a href="/wiki/Eastern_Orthodox_Church" title="Eastern Orthodox Church">Eastern Orthodox</a> and <a href="/wiki/Western_Catholic_Church" class="mw-redirect" title="Western Catholic Church">Western Catholic Church</a> that is reflected in Albania through the emergence of a Catholic north and Orthodox south. The Albanian people inhabited the west of <a href="/wiki/Lake_Ochrida" class="mw-redirect" title="Lake Ochrida">Lake Ochrida</a> and the upper valley of <a href="/wiki/Shkumbin" title="Shkumbin">River Shkumbin</a> and established the <a href="/wiki/Principality_of_Arbanon" title="Principality of Arbanon">Principality of Arbanon</a> in 1190 under the leadership of <a href="/wiki/Progon_of_Kruja" class="mw-redirect" title="Progon of Kruja">Progon of Kruja</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-45" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-45">&#91;43&#93;</a></sup> The realm was succeeded by his sons <a href="/wiki/Gjin_Progoni" title="Gjin Progoni">Gjin</a> and Dhimitri.
</p><p>Upon the death of Dhimiter, the territory came under the rule of the Albanian-Greek <a href="/wiki/Gregory_Kamonas" class="mw-redirect" title="Gregory Kamonas">Gregory Kamonas</a> and subsequently under the <a href="/wiki/Golem_of_Kruja" title="Golem of Kruja">Golem of Kruja</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-46" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-46">&#91;44&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Abulafia_47-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Abulafia-47">&#91;45&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Genealogist_48-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Genealogist-48">&#91;46&#93;</a></sup> In the 13th century, the principality was dissolved.<sup id="cite_ref-Clements31_49-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Clements31-49">&#91;47&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-PickardÇeliku2008_50-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-PickardÇeliku2008-50">&#91;48&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Norris1993_51-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Norris1993-51">&#91;49&#93;</a></sup> Arbanon is considered to be the first sketch of an Albanian state, that retained a <a href="/wiki/Semi-autonomous" class="mw-redirect" title="Semi-autonomous">semi-autonomous</a> status as the western extremity of the <a href="/wiki/Byzantine_Empire" title="Byzantine Empire">Byzantine Empire</a>, under the Byzantine <a href="/wiki/Doukas" title="Doukas">Doukai</a> of <a href="/wiki/Despotate_of_Epirus" title="Despotate of Epirus">Epirus</a> or <a href="/wiki/Laskaris" title="Laskaris">Laskarids</a> of <a href="/wiki/Empire_of_Nicaea" title="Empire of Nicaea">Nicaea</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-52" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-52">&#91;50&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Venezia_-_Ex_Scola_degli_albanesi_(sec._XV)_-_Foto_Giovanni_Dall%27Orto,_12-Aug-2007_-_11_-_Maometto_II_assedia_Scutari.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d1/Venezia_-_Ex_Scola_degli_albanesi_%28sec._XV%29_-_Foto_Giovanni_Dall%27Orto%2C_12-Aug-2007_-_11_-_Maometto_II_assedia_Scutari.jpg/220px-Venezia_-_Ex_Scola_degli_albanesi_%28sec._XV%29_-_Foto_Giovanni_Dall%27Orto%2C_12-Aug-2007_-_11_-_Maometto_II_assedia_Scutari.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="165" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d1/Venezia_-_Ex_Scola_degli_albanesi_%28sec._XV%29_-_Foto_Giovanni_Dall%27Orto%2C_12-Aug-2007_-_11_-_Maometto_II_assedia_Scutari.jpg/330px-Venezia_-_Ex_Scola_degli_albanesi_%28sec._XV%29_-_Foto_Giovanni_Dall%27Orto%2C_12-Aug-2007_-_11_-_Maometto_II_assedia_Scutari.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d1/Venezia_-_Ex_Scola_degli_albanesi_%28sec._XV%29_-_Foto_Giovanni_Dall%27Orto%2C_12-Aug-2007_-_11_-_Maometto_II_assedia_Scutari.jpg/440px-Venezia_-_Ex_Scola_degli_albanesi_%28sec._XV%29_-_Foto_Giovanni_Dall%27Orto%2C_12-Aug-2007_-_11_-_Maometto_II_assedia_Scutari.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2592" data-file-height="1944" /></a><figcaption>A relief of the <a href="/wiki/Scuola_degli_Albanesi" title="Scuola degli Albanesi">Scuola degli Albanesi</a> commemorating the <a href="/wiki/Siege_of_Shkodra" title="Siege of Shkodra">siege of Shkodra</a>. It illustrates <a href="/wiki/Ottoman_Sultan" class="mw-redirect" title="Ottoman Sultan">Sultan</a> <a href="/wiki/Mehmet_II" class="mw-redirect" title="Mehmet II">Mehmet II</a> laying siege to the Albanian town of Scutari, then part of <a href="/wiki/Venetian_Empire" class="mw-redirect" title="Venetian Empire">Venetian Empire</a>.</figcaption></figure>
<p>Towards the end of the 12th and beginning of the 13th centuries, <a href="/wiki/Kingdom_of_Serbia_(medieval)" title="Kingdom of Serbia (medieval)">Serbs</a> and <a href="/wiki/Venetian_Empire" class="mw-redirect" title="Venetian Empire">Venetians</a> started to take possession over the territory.<sup id="cite_ref-Barbarian_Invasions_53-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Barbarian_Invasions-53">&#91;51&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Ethnogenesis" title="Ethnogenesis">ethnogenesis</a> of the Albanians is uncertain; however, the first undisputed mention of Albanians dates back in historical records from 1079 or 1080 in a work by <a href="/wiki/Michael_Attaliates" class="mw-redirect" title="Michael Attaliates">Michael Attaliates</a>, who referred to the <a href="/wiki/Albanoi" title="Albanoi">Albanoi</a> as having taken part in a revolt against <a href="/wiki/Constantinople" title="Constantinople">Constantinople</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-54" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-54">&#91;52&#93;</a></sup> At this point the Albanians were fully Christianised.
</p><p>After the dissolution of Arbanon, <a href="/wiki/Charles_I_of_Naples" class="mw-redirect" title="Charles I of Naples">Charles of Anjou</a> concluded an agreement with the Albanian rulers, promising to protect them and their ancient liberties. In 1272, he established the <a href="/wiki/Kingdom_of_Albania_(medieval)" title="Kingdom of Albania (medieval)">Kingdom of Albania</a> and conquered regions back from the <a href="/wiki/Despotate_of_Epirus" title="Despotate of Epirus">Despotate of Epirus</a>. The kingdom claimed all of central Albania territory from <a href="/wiki/Dyrrhachium" class="mw-redirect" title="Dyrrhachium">Dyrrhachium</a> along the Adriatic Sea coast down to <a href="/wiki/Butrint" title="Butrint">Butrint</a>. A catholic political structure was a basis for the papal plans of spreading <a href="/wiki/Catholicism" class="mw-redirect" title="Catholicism">Catholicism</a> in the Balkan Peninsula. This plan found also the support of <a href="/wiki/Helen_of_Anjou" title="Helen of Anjou">Helen of Anjou</a>, a cousin of Charles of Anjou. Around 30 Catholic churches and monasteries were built during her rule mainly in northern Albania.<sup id="cite_ref-55" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-55">&#91;53&#93;</a></sup> Internal power struggles within the Byzantine Empire in the 14th century enabled Serbs' most powerful medieval ruler, <a href="/wiki/Stefan_Dusan" class="mw-redirect" title="Stefan Dusan">Stefan Dusan</a>, to establish a <a href="/wiki/Serbian_Empire" title="Serbian Empire">short-lived empire</a> that included all of Albania except Durrës.<sup id="cite_ref-Barbarian_Invasions_53-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Barbarian_Invasions-53">&#91;51&#93;</a></sup> In 1367, various Albanian rulers established the <a href="/wiki/Despotate_of_Arta" title="Despotate of Arta">Despotate of Arta</a>. During that time, several <a href="/wiki/Albanian_principalities" title="Albanian principalities">Albanian principalities</a> were created, notably the <a href="/wiki/Principality_of_Albania_(medieval)" title="Principality of Albania (medieval)">Principality of Albania</a>, <a href="/wiki/Principality_of_Kastrioti" title="Principality of Kastrioti">Principality of Kastrioti</a>, <a href="/wiki/Lordship_of_Berat" class="mw-redirect" title="Lordship of Berat">Lordship of Berat</a> and <a href="/wiki/Principality_of_Dukagjini" title="Principality of Dukagjini">Principality of Dukagjini</a>. In the first half of the 15th century, the <a href="/wiki/Ottoman_Empire" title="Ottoman Empire">Ottoman Empire</a> invaded most of Albania, and the <a href="/wiki/League_of_Lezh%C3%AB" title="League of Lezhë">League of Lezhë</a> was held under <a href="/wiki/Skanderbeg" title="Skanderbeg">Skanderbeg</a> as a ruler, who became the national hero of the Albanian medieval history.
</p>
<h4><span class="mw-headline" id="Ottoman_Empire">Ottoman Empire</span></h4>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Albania_under_the_Ottoman_Empire" title="Albania under the Ottoman Empire">Albania under the Ottoman Empire</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/Skanderbeg#Rebellion_against_the_Ottomans" title="Skanderbeg">Albanian rebellion against the Ottoman Empire</a></div>

was a powerful autonomous Ottoman-Albanian ruler, governing over the <a href="/wiki/Pashalik_of_Yanina" title="Pashalik of Yanina">Pashalik of Yanina</a>.</div></div></div></div></div>
<p>With the <a href="/wiki/Fall_of_Constantinople" title="Fall of Constantinople">fall of Constantinople</a>, the Ottoman Empire continued an extended period of conquest and expansion with its borders going deep into <a href="/wiki/Ottoman_conquest_of_the_Balkans" class="mw-redirect" title="Ottoman conquest of the Balkans">Southeast Europe</a>. They reached the <a href="/wiki/Albanian_Ionian_Sea_Coast" title="Albanian Ionian Sea Coast">Albanian Ionian Sea Coast</a> in 1385 and erected their garrisons across <a href="/wiki/Southern_Albania" title="Southern Albania">Southern Albania</a> in 1415 and then occupied most of Albania in 1431.<sup id="cite_ref-56" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-56">&#91;54&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Hupchich110_57-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Hupchich110-57">&#91;55&#93;</a></sup> Thousands of Albanians consequently fled to Western Europe, particularly to <a href="/wiki/Calabria" title="Calabria">Calabria</a>, <a href="/wiki/Kingdom_of_Naples" title="Kingdom of Naples">Naples</a>, <a href="/wiki/Republic_of_Ragusa" title="Republic of Ragusa">Ragusa</a> and <a href="/wiki/Kingdom_of_Sicily" title="Kingdom of Sicily">Sicily</a>, whereby others sought protection at the often inaccessible <a href="/wiki/Geography_of_Albania" title="Geography of Albania">Mountains of Albania</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-58" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-58">&#91;56&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-59" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-59">&#91;57&#93;</a></sup> The Albanians, as Christians, were considered an <a href="/wiki/Rayah" title="Rayah">inferior class</a> of people, and as such they were subjected to heavy <a href="/wiki/Jizya" title="Jizya">taxes</a> among others by the <a href="/wiki/Devshirme" title="Devshirme">Devshirme</a> system that allowed the <a href="/wiki/Sultan" title="Sultan">Sultan</a> to collect a requisite percentage of Christian adolescents from their families to compose the <a href="/wiki/Janissary" title="Janissary">Janissary</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-60" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-60">&#91;58&#93;</a></sup> The Ottoman conquest was also accompanied with the gradual process of <a href="/wiki/Islamisation" class="mw-redirect" title="Islamisation">Islamisation</a> and the rapid construction of mosques.
</p><p>A prosperous and longstanding revolution erupted after the formation of the <a href="/wiki/League_of_Lezh%C3%AB" title="League of Lezhë">Assembly of Lezhë</a> until the <a href="/wiki/Siege_of_Shkodra" title="Siege of Shkodra">Siege of Shkodër</a> under the leadership of <a href="/wiki/Gjergj_Kastrioti_Skanderbeg" class="mw-redirect" title="Gjergj Kastrioti Skanderbeg">Gjergj Kastrioti Skanderbeg</a>, multiple times defeating major Ottoman armies led by <a href="/wiki/Sultan" title="Sultan">Sultans</a> <a href="/wiki/Murad_II" title="Murad II">Murad II</a> and <a href="/wiki/Mehmed_II" title="Mehmed II">Mehmed II</a>. Skanderbeg managed to gather several of the Albanian principals, amongst them the <a href="/wiki/Arianiti_family" title="Arianiti family">Arianitis</a>, <a href="/wiki/Dukagjini_family" title="Dukagjini family">Dukagjinis</a>, <a href="/wiki/Zaharia_family" title="Zaharia family">Zaharias</a> and <a href="/wiki/Thopia_family" title="Thopia family">Thopias</a>, and establish a centralised authority over most of the non-conquered territories, becoming the <a href="/wiki/Skanderbeg" title="Skanderbeg">Lord of Albania</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-League_of_Lezhë_61-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-League_of_Lezhë-61">&#91;59&#93;</a></sup> Skanderbeg consistently pursued the goal relentlessly but rather unsuccessfully to constitute a European coalition against the Ottomans. He thwarted every attempt by the Ottomans to regain Albania, which they envisioned as a springboard for the invasion of Western Europe. His unequal fight against them won financial and military aid from the <a href="/wiki/Papacy" class="mw-redirect" title="Papacy">Papacy</a> and <a href="/wiki/Kingdom_of_Naples" title="Kingdom of Naples">Naples</a>, <a href="/wiki/Republic_of_Venice" title="Republic of Venice">Venice</a> and <a href="/wiki/Republic_of_Ragusa" title="Republic of Ragusa">Ragusa</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-britannica_62-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-britannica-62">&#91;60&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>When the Ottomans were gaining a firm foothold in the region, Albanian towns were organised into four principal <a href="/wiki/Sanjaks" class="mw-redirect" title="Sanjaks">sanjaks</a>. The government fostered trade by settling a sizeable Jewish colony of refugees fleeing persecution in Spain. The city of <a href="/wiki/Vlor%C3%AB" title="Vlorë">Vlorë</a> saw passing through its ports imported merchandise from Europe such as velvets, cotton goods, mohairs, carpets, spices and leather from <a href="/wiki/Bursa" title="Bursa">Bursa</a> and <a href="/wiki/Constantinople" title="Constantinople">Constantinople</a>. Some citizens of Vlorë even had business associates throughout Europe.<sup id="cite_ref-Arnawutlu_63-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Arnawutlu-63">&#91;61&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The phenomenon of Islamisation among the Albanians became primarily widespread from the 17th century and continued into the 18th century.<sup id="cite_ref-referenceworks.brillonline_64-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-referenceworks.brillonline-64">&#91;62&#93;</a></sup> Islam offered them equal opportunities and advancement within the Ottoman Empire. However, motives for conversion were, according to some scholars, diverse depending on the context though the lack of source material does not help when investigating such issues.<sup id="cite_ref-referenceworks.brillonline_64-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-referenceworks.brillonline-64">&#91;62&#93;</a></sup> Because of increasing suppression of Catholicism, most Catholic Albanians converted in the 17th century, while Orthodox Albanians followed suit mainly in the following century.
</p><p>Since the Albanians were seen as strategically important, they made up a significant proportion of the <a href="/wiki/Ottoman_military" class="mw-redirect" title="Ottoman military">Ottoman military</a> and bureaucracy. Many Muslim Albanians attained important political and military positions and culturally contributed to the broader <a href="/wiki/Muslim_world" title="Muslim world">Muslim world</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-referenceworks.brillonline_64-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-referenceworks.brillonline-64">&#91;62&#93;</a></sup> Enjoying this privileged position, they held various high administrative positions with over two dozen Albanian <a href="/wiki/Grand_Viziers" class="mw-redirect" title="Grand Viziers">Grand Viziers</a>. Others included members of the prominent <a href="/wiki/K%C3%B6pr%C3%BCl%C3%BC_family" title="Köprülü family">Köprülü family</a>, <a href="/wiki/Zagan_Pasha" title="Zagan Pasha">Zagan Pasha</a>, <a href="/wiki/Muhammad_Ali_of_Egypt" class="mw-redirect" title="Muhammad Ali of Egypt">Muhammad Ali of Egypt</a> and <a href="/wiki/Ali_Pasha_of_Tepelena" class="mw-redirect" title="Ali Pasha of Tepelena">Ali Pasha of Tepelena</a>. Furthermore, two sultans, <a href="/wiki/Bayezid_II" title="Bayezid II">Bayezid II</a> and <a href="/wiki/Mehmed_III" title="Mehmed III">Mehmed III</a>, both had mothers of Albanian origin.<sup id="cite_ref-Arnawutlu_63-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Arnawutlu-63">&#91;61&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-65" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-65">&#91;63&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-66" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-66">&#91;64&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Rilindja">Rilindja</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Albanian_Renaissance" class="mw-redirect" title="Albanian Renaissance">Albanian Renaissance</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/League_of_Prizren" title="League of Prizren">League of Prizren</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1096954695/mw-parser-output/.tmulti"><div class="thumb tmulti tright"><div class="thumbinner multiimageinner" style="width:222px;max-width:222px"><div class="trow"><div class="tsingle" style="width:108px;max-width:108px"><div class="thumbimage" style="border:none;;height:148px;overflow:hidden"><span typeof="mw:File"><a href="/wiki/File:NaumVeqilharxhi.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="Naum Veqilharxhi" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/da/NaumVeqilharxhi.jpg/106px-NaumVeqilharxhi.jpg" decoding="async" width="106" height="149" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/da/NaumVeqilharxhi.jpg/159px-NaumVeqilharxhi.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/da/NaumVeqilharxhi.jpg/212px-NaumVeqilharxhi.jpg 2x" data-file-width="689" data-file-height="967" /></a></span></div><div class="thumbcaption"><a href="/wiki/Naum_Veqilharxhi" title="Naum Veqilharxhi">Naum Veqilharxhi</a> was among the most important figures of the early <a href="/wiki/Albanian_National_Awakening" title="Albanian National Awakening">Albanian Renaissance</a>.</div></div><div class="tsingle" style="width:110px;max-width:110px"><div class="thumbimage" style="border:none;;height:148px;overflow:hidden"><span typeof="mw:File"><a href="/wiki/File:Dora_d%27Istria_(drawing).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="Dora d&#39;Istria" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/68/Dora_d%27Istria_%28drawing%29.jpg/108px-Dora_d%27Istria_%28drawing%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="108" height="148" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/68/Dora_d%27Istria_%28drawing%29.jpg/162px-Dora_d%27Istria_%28drawing%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/68/Dora_d%27Istria_%28drawing%29.jpg/216px-Dora_d%27Istria_%28drawing%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="505" data-file-height="694" /></a></span></div><div class="thumbcaption"><a href="/wiki/Dora_d%27Istria" title="Dora d&#39;Istria">Dora d'Istria</a> was among the main advocates in Europe for the <a href="/wiki/Albanian_Renaissance" class="mw-redirect" title="Albanian Renaissance">Albanian cause</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-67" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-67">&#91;65&#93;</a></sup></div></div></div></div></div>
<p>The <a href="/wiki/Albanian_Renaissance" class="mw-redirect" title="Albanian Renaissance">Albanian Renaissance</a> was a period with its roots in the late 18th century and continuing into the 19th century, during which the Albanian people gathered spiritual and intellectual strength for an independent cultural and political life within an <a href="/wiki/Independent_Albania" title="Independent Albania">independent nation</a>. Modern <a href="/wiki/Albanian_culture" class="mw-redirect" title="Albanian culture">Albanian culture</a> flourished too, especially <a href="/wiki/Albanian_literature" title="Albanian literature">Albanian literature</a> and <a href="/wiki/Albanian_art" title="Albanian art">arts</a>, and was frequently linked to the influences of the <a href="/wiki/Romanticism" title="Romanticism">Romanticism</a> and <a href="/wiki/Age_of_Enlightenment" title="Age of Enlightenment">Enlightenment</a> principles.<sup id="cite_ref-68" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-68">&#91;66&#93;</a></sup> Prior to the <a href="/wiki/Rise_of_nationalism_in_the_Ottoman_Empire" title="Rise of nationalism in the Ottoman Empire">rise of nationalism</a>, Ottoman authorities suppressed any expression of national unity or conscience by the Albanian people.
</p><p>The victory of Russia over the Ottoman Empire following the <a href="/wiki/Russian-Ottoman_War" class="mw-redirect" title="Russian-Ottoman War">Russian-Ottoman Wars</a> resulted the execution of the <a href="/wiki/Treaty_of_San_Stefano" title="Treaty of San Stefano">Treaty of San Stefano</a> which overlooked to assign Albanian-populated lands to the Slavic and Greek neighbours. However, the <a href="/wiki/United_Kingdom_of_Great_Britain_and_Ireland" title="United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland">United Kingdom</a> and <a href="/wiki/Austro-Hungarian_Empire" class="mw-redirect" title="Austro-Hungarian Empire">Austro-Hungarian Empire</a> consequently blocked the arrangement and caused the <a href="/wiki/Treaty_of_Berlin_(1878)" title="Treaty of Berlin (1878)">Treaty of Berlin</a>. From this point, Albanians started to organise themselves with the goal to protect and unite the Albanian-populated lands into a unitary nation, leading to the formation of the <a href="/wiki/League_of_Prizren" title="League of Prizren">League of Prizren</a>. The league had initially the assistance of the Ottoman authorities whose position was based on the religious solidarity of Muslim people and landlords connected with the <a href="/wiki/Ottoman_Porte" class="mw-redirect" title="Ottoman Porte">Ottoman administration</a>. They favoured and protected the Muslim solidarity and called for defence of Muslim lands simultaneously constituting the reason for titling the league <a href="/wiki/League_of_Prizren#Formation" title="League of Prizren">Committee of the Real Muslims</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-69" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-69">&#91;67&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Approximately 300 Muslims participated in the assembly composed by delegates from Bosnia, the <a href="/wiki/Sanjakbey" class="mw-redirect" title="Sanjakbey">administrator</a> of the <a href="/wiki/Sanjak_of_Prizren" title="Sanjak of Prizren">Sanjak of Prizren</a> as representatives of the central authorities and no delegates from <a href="/wiki/Vilayet_of_Scutari" class="mw-redirect" title="Vilayet of Scutari">Vilayet of Scutari</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-70" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-70">&#91;68&#93;</a></sup> Signed by only 47 Muslim deputies, the league issued the <a href="/wiki/Kararname_(League_of_Prizren)" title="Kararname (League of Prizren)">Kararname</a> that contained a proclamation that the people from northern Albania, <a href="/wiki/Epirus" title="Epirus">Epirus</a> and <a href="/wiki/Bosnia_and_Herzegovina" title="Bosnia and Herzegovina">Bosnia and Herzegovina</a> are willing to defend the <a href="/wiki/Territorial_integrity" title="Territorial integrity">territorial integrity</a> of the Ottoman Empire by all possible means against the troops of <a href="/wiki/Kingdom_of_Bulgaria" title="Kingdom of Bulgaria">Bulgaria</a>, <a href="/wiki/Kingdom_of_Serbia" title="Kingdom of Serbia">Serbia</a> and <a href="/wiki/Kingdom_of_Montenegro" title="Kingdom of Montenegro">Montenegro</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-albanianhistory.net_71-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-albanianhistory.net-71">&#91;69&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Ottomans authorities cancelled their assistance when the league, under <a href="/wiki/Abdyl_Frash%C3%ABri" title="Abdyl Frashëri">Abdyl Frashëri</a>, became focused on working towards Albanian autonomy and requested merging four <a href="/wiki/Ottoman_vilayet" class="mw-redirect" title="Ottoman vilayet">vilayets</a>, including <a href="/wiki/Kosovo_Vilayet" class="mw-redirect" title="Kosovo Vilayet">Kosovo</a>, <a href="/wiki/Scutari_Vilayet" class="mw-redirect" title="Scutari Vilayet">Shkodër</a>, <a href="/wiki/Monastir_Vilayet" class="mw-redirect" title="Monastir Vilayet">Monastir</a> and <a href="/wiki/Janina_Vilayet" class="mw-redirect" title="Janina Vilayet">Ioannina</a>, into an unified vilayet, the <a href="/wiki/Albanian_Vilayet" title="Albanian Vilayet">Albanian Vilayet</a>. The league used military force to prevent the annexing areas of <a href="/wiki/Plav_Municipality" title="Plav Municipality">Plav</a> and <a href="/wiki/Gusinje" title="Gusinje">Gusinje</a> assigned to Montenegro. After several successful battles with Montenegrin troops, such as the <a href="/wiki/Battle_of_Nov%C5%A1i%C4%87e" title="Battle of Novšiće">Battle of Novšiće</a>, the league was forced to retreat from their contested regions. The league was later defeated by the Ottoman army sent by the sultan.<sup id="cite_ref-League_of_Prizren_72-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-League_of_Prizren-72">&#91;70&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<div style="clear:both;"></div>
<h4><span class="mw-headline" id="Independence">Independence</span></h4>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Independent_Albania" title="Independent Albania">Independent Albania</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/Albanian_Declaration_of_Independence" title="Albanian Declaration of Independence">Albanian Declaration of Independence</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Further information: <a href="/wiki/Massacres_of_Albanians_in_the_Balkan_Wars" title="Massacres of Albanians in the Balkan Wars">Massacres of Albanians in the Balkan Wars</a></div>
<figure class="mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Ismail_Qemali_(portrait).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8e/Ismail_Qemali_%28portrait%29.jpg/175px-Ismail_Qemali_%28portrait%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="175" height="234" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8e/Ismail_Qemali_%28portrait%29.jpg/263px-Ismail_Qemali_%28portrait%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8e/Ismail_Qemali_%28portrait%29.jpg/350px-Ismail_Qemali_%28portrait%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="457" data-file-height="611" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Ismail_Qemali" title="Ismail Qemali">Ismail Qemali</a> is regarded as the <a href="/wiki/List_of_national_founders#Albania" title="List of national founders">founding father</a> of the modern Albanian nation.</figcaption></figure>
<p>Albania <a href="/wiki/Albanian_Declaration_of_Independence" title="Albanian Declaration of Independence">declared independence</a> from the Ottoman Empire on 28 November 1912, accompanied with the establishment of the <a href="/wiki/Senate_of_Albania" class="mw-redirect" title="Senate of Albania">Senate</a> and <a href="/wiki/Provisional_Government_of_Albania" title="Provisional Government of Albania">Government</a> by the <a href="/wiki/Assembly_of_Vlor%C3%AB" title="Assembly of Vlorë">Assembly of Vlorë</a> on 4 December 1912.<sup id="cite_ref-73" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-73">&#91;71&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-74" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-74">&#91;72&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-75" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-75">&#91;73&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-76" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-76">&#91;74&#93;</a></sup> Its sovereignty was recognised by the <a href="/wiki/London_Conference_of_1912%E2%80%931913" title="London Conference of 1912–1913">Conference of London</a>. On 29 July 1913, the <a href="/wiki/Treaty_of_London_(1913)" title="Treaty of London (1913)">Treaty of London</a> delineated the borders of the country and its neighbours, leaving many Albanians outside Albania, predominantly <a href="/wiki/Partition_(politics)" title="Partition (politics)">partitioned</a> between <a href="/wiki/Kingdom_of_Montenegro" title="Kingdom of Montenegro">Montenegro</a>, <a href="/wiki/Kingdom_of_Serbia" title="Kingdom of Serbia">Serbia</a> and <a href="/wiki/Kingdom_of_Greece" title="Kingdom of Greece">Greece</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-77" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-77">&#91;75&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Headquartered in Vlorë, the <a href="/wiki/International_Commission_of_Control" class="mw-redirect" title="International Commission of Control">International Commission of Control</a> was established on 15 October 1913 to take care of the administration of newly established Albania, until its own political institutions were in order.<sup id="cite_ref-78" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-78">&#91;76&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-79" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-79">&#91;77&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/International_Gendarmerie" title="International Gendarmerie">International Gendarmerie</a> was established as the first law enforcement agency of the <a href="/wiki/Principality_of_Albania" title="Principality of Albania">Principality of Albania</a>. In November, the first gendarmerie members arrived in the country. Prince of Albania <a href="/wiki/Wilhelm_of_Wied" class="mw-redirect" title="Wilhelm of Wied">Wilhelm of Wied</a> <i>(Princ Vilhelm Vidi)</i> was selected as the first prince of the principality.<sup id="cite_ref-80" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-80">&#91;78&#93;</a></sup> On 7 March, he arrived in the provisional capital of <a href="/wiki/Durr%C3%ABs" title="Durrës">Durrës</a> and started to organise his government, appointing <a href="/wiki/Turhan_Pasha_P%C3%ABrmeti" class="mw-redirect" title="Turhan Pasha Përmeti">Turhan Pasha Përmeti</a> to form the first Albanian cabinet.
</p><p>In November 1913, the Albanian pro-Ottoman forces had offered the throne of Albania to the Ottoman war Minister of Albanian origin, <a href="/wiki/Ahmed_Izzet_Pasha" title="Ahmed Izzet Pasha">Ahmed Izzet Pasha</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-81" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-81">&#91;79&#93;</a></sup> The pro-Ottoman peasants believed that the new regime was a tool of the six Christian <a href="/wiki/Great_Power" class="mw-redirect" title="Great Power">Great Powers</a> and local landowners, that owned half of the arable land.<sup id="cite_ref-82" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-82">&#91;80&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In February 1914, the <a href="/wiki/Autonomous_Republic_of_Northern_Epirus" title="Autonomous Republic of Northern Epirus">Autonomous Republic of Northern Epirus</a> was proclaimed in <a href="/wiki/Gjirokast%C3%ABr" title="Gjirokastër">Gjirokastër</a> by the local <a href="/wiki/Greeks_in_Albania" title="Greeks in Albania">Greek population</a> against incorporation to Albania. This initiative was short-lived, and in 1921 the southern provinces were incorporated into the Albanian Principality.<sup id="cite_ref-83" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-83">&#91;81&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-84" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-84">&#91;82&#93;</a></sup> Meanwhile, the <a href="/wiki/Peasant_Revolt_in_Albania" title="Peasant Revolt in Albania">revolt of Albanian peasants</a> against the new Albanian regime erupted under the leadership of the group of Muslim clerics gathered around <a href="/wiki/Essad_Pasha_Toptani" title="Essad Pasha Toptani">Essad Pasha Toptani</a>, who proclaimed himself the saviour of Albania and Islam.<sup id="cite_ref-85" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-85">&#91;83&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-86" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-86">&#91;84&#93;</a></sup> In order to gain support of the <a href="/wiki/Mirdita" title="Mirdita">Mirdita</a> Catholic volunteers from the northern part of Albania, Prince <a href="/wiki/Wilhelm_of_Wied" class="mw-redirect" title="Wilhelm of Wied">Wied</a> appointed their leader, <a href="/wiki/Pr%C3%AAnk_Bib%C3%AB_Doda" class="mw-redirect" title="Prênk Bibë Doda">Prênk Bibë Doda</a>, to be the foreign minister of the Principality of Albania. In May and June 1914, the International Gendarmerie was joined by <a href="/wiki/Isa_Boletini" title="Isa Boletini">Isa Boletini</a> and his men, mostly from <a href="/wiki/Kosovo" title="Kosovo">Kosovo</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-87" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-87">&#91;85&#93;</a></sup> and northern <a href="/wiki/Mirdita" title="Mirdita">Mirdita</a> Catholics, were defeated by the rebels who captured most of Central Albania by the end of August 1914.<sup id="cite_ref-88" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-88">&#91;86&#93;</a></sup> The regime of Prince Wied collapsed, and he left the country on 3 September 1914.<sup id="cite_ref-89" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-89">&#91;87&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="First_Republic_and_Kingdom">First Republic and Kingdom</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Albanian_Republic_(1925%E2%80%931928)" title="Albanian Republic (1925–1928)">First Republic of Albania</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/World_War_II_in_Albania" title="World War II in Albania">World War II in Albania</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Further information: <a href="/wiki/The_Holocaust_in_Albania" title="The Holocaust in Albania">The Holocaust in Albania</a> and <a href="/wiki/List_of_Albanian_Righteous_Among_the_Nations" class="mw-redirect" title="List of Albanian Righteous Among the Nations">Albanian Righteous Among the Nations</a></div>
<figure class="mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:King_Zog.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8e/King_Zog.jpg/175px-King_Zog.jpg" decoding="async" width="175" height="236" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8e/King_Zog.jpg/263px-King_Zog.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8e/King_Zog.jpg/350px-King_Zog.jpg 2x" data-file-width="3820" data-file-height="5158" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Zog_I_of_Albania" title="Zog I of Albania">Zog I</a> was the first and only king of Albania; his reign lasted 11 years (1928–1939).</figcaption></figure>
<p>Following the end of the government of <a href="/wiki/Fan_Noli" title="Fan Noli">Fan Noli</a>, the parliament adopted a new constitution and proclaimed the country as a parliamentary republic in which King <a href="/wiki/Zog_I_of_Albania" title="Zog I of Albania">Zog I of Albania</a> (Ahmet Muhtar Zogu) served as the <a href="/wiki/Head_of_state" title="Head of state">head of state</a> for a seven-year term. <a href="/wiki/Tirana" title="Tirana">Tirana</a> was endorsed officially as the country's permanent capital.<sup id="cite_ref-90" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-90">&#91;88&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The politics of Zogu was authoritarian and conservative with the primary aim of the maintenance of stability and order. He was forced to adopt a policy of cooperation with Italy where a pact had been signed between both countries, whereby Italy gained a monopoly on shipping and trade concessions.<sup id="cite_ref-Vickers_91-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Vickers-91">&#91;89&#93;</a></sup> Italians exercised control over nearly every Albanian official through money and patronage.<sup id="cite_ref-Gerwarth_92-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Gerwarth-92">&#91;90&#93;</a></sup> In 1928, the Albanian regime was replaced by <a href="/wiki/Kingdom_of_Albania_(1928%E2%80%931939)" class="mw-redirect" title="Kingdom of Albania (1928–1939)">another monarchy</a> that enjoyed strong support from <a href="/wiki/Fascist_Italy_(1922%E2%80%931943)" title="Fascist Italy (1922–1943)">Fascist Italy</a>, with which it maintained close relations until the <a href="/wiki/Italian_invasion_of_Albania" title="Italian invasion of Albania">Italian invasion</a> of the country. Zogu remained a conservative but initiated reforms and placed great emphasis on the development of infrastructure. He also made donations of land to international organisations for the building of schools and hospitals. The armed forces were trained and supervised by instructors from Italy, and as a counterweight, he kept British officers in the <a href="/wiki/Gendarmerie" title="Gendarmerie">Gendarmerie</a> despite strong Italian pressure to remove them.
</p><p>After being militarily occupied by Italy from 1939 until 1943, the <a href="/wiki/Albanian_Kingdom_(1939%E2%80%9343)" class="mw-redirect" title="Albanian Kingdom (1939–43)">Kingdom of Albania</a> was a <a href="/wiki/Protectorate" title="Protectorate">protectorate</a> and a <a href="/wiki/Dependent_territory" title="Dependent territory">dependency</a> of the <a href="/wiki/Kingdom_of_Italy" title="Kingdom of Italy">Kingdom of Italy</a> governed by <a href="/wiki/Victor_Emmanuel_III_of_Italy" title="Victor Emmanuel III of Italy">Victor Emmanuel III</a> and his government. In October 1940, Albania served as a staging ground for an unsuccessful Italian <a href="/wiki/Greco-Italian_War" title="Greco-Italian War">invasion of Greece</a>. A counterattack resulted in a sizeable portion of southern Albania coming under Greek military control until April 1941 when Greece capitulated during the <a href="/wiki/Battle_of_Greece" class="mw-redirect" title="Battle of Greece">German invasion</a>. In April 1941, territories of <a href="/wiki/Kingdom_of_Yugoslavia" title="Kingdom of Yugoslavia">Yugoslavia</a> with substantial Albanian population were annexed to Albania inclusively western Macedonia, a strip of eastern Montenegro, the town of <a href="/wiki/Tutin,_Serbia" title="Tutin, Serbia">Tutin</a> in central Serbia and most of Kosovo.<sup id="cite_ref-BogdaniLoughlin2007_93-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-BogdaniLoughlin2007-93">&#91;91&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Germans started to occupy the country in September 1943 and subsequently announced that they would recognise the independence of a neutral Albania and set about organising a new government, military and law enforcement. <a href="/wiki/Balli_Komb%C3%ABtar" title="Balli Kombëtar">Balli Kombëtar</a> formed a neutral government and side by side with the Germans fought against the communist-led <a href="/wiki/National_Liberation_Movement_(Albania)" title="National Liberation Movement (Albania)">National Liberation Movement</a> of Albania.<sup id="cite_ref-Morrock2010_94-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Morrock2010-94">&#91;92&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>During the last years of the war, the country fell into a civil war-like state between the communists and nationalists. The communists defeated the last anti-communist forces in the south in 1944. Before the end of November, the main German troops had withdrawn from Tirana, and the communists took control by attacking it. The partisans entirely liberated the country from German occupation on 29 November 1944. A provisional government, which the communists had formed at&#160;Berat&#160;in October, administered Albania with <a href="/wiki/Enver_Hoxha" title="Enver Hoxha">Enver Hoxha</a> as the head of government.
</p><p>By the end of the <a href="/wiki/Second_World_War" class="mw-redirect" title="Second World War">Second World War</a>, the main military and political force of the nation, the Communist party sent forces to northern Albania against the nationalists to eliminate its rivals. They faced open resistance in <a href="/wiki/Nikaj-M%C3%ABrtur_region" title="Nikaj-Mërtur region">Nikaj-Mërtur</a>, <a href="/wiki/Dukagjin_Highlands" title="Dukagjin Highlands">Dukagjin</a> and <a href="/wiki/Kelmendi_(tribe)" title="Kelmendi (tribe)">Kelmend</a> led by <a href="/wiki/Prek_Cali" title="Prek Cali">Prek Cali</a>.<sup class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">&#91;<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><span title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (April 2020)">citation needed</span></a></i>&#93;</sup> On 15 January 1945, a clash took place between partisans of the first Brigade and nationalist forces at the Tamara Bridge, resulting in the defeat of the nationalist forces. About 150 <a href="/wiki/Kelmendi_(tribe)" title="Kelmendi (tribe)">Kelmendi</a><sup id="cite_ref-95" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-95">&#91;93&#93;</a></sup> people were killed or tortured. This event was the starting point of many other issues which took place during <a href="/wiki/Enver_Hoxha" title="Enver Hoxha">Enver Hoxha</a>'s dictatorship. <a href="/wiki/Class_conflict" title="Class conflict">Class struggle</a> was strictly applied, human freedom and human rights were denied.<sup id="cite_ref-Albanian_Nationalism_96-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Albanian_Nationalism-96">&#91;94&#93;</a></sup> The Kelmend region was almost isolated by both the border and by a lack of roads for another 20 years, the institution of <a href="/wiki/Agricultural_cooperative" title="Agricultural cooperative">agricultural cooperatives</a> brought about economic decline. Many Kelmendi people fled, and some were executed trying to cross the border.<sup id="cite_ref-Albanian_Nationalism_96-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Albanian_Nationalism-96">&#91;94&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<div style="clear:both;"></div>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Communism">Communism</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Communism_in_Albania" class="mw-redirect" title="Communism in Albania">Communism in Albania</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Further information: <a href="/wiki/Bunkers_in_Albania" title="Bunkers in Albania">Bunkers in Albania</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:HOD%C5%BDA_druh%C3%A1_m%C3%ADza_crop.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fa/HOD%C5%BDA_druh%C3%A1_m%C3%ADza_crop.jpg/170px-HOD%C5%BDA_druh%C3%A1_m%C3%ADza_crop.jpg" decoding="async" width="170" height="229" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fa/HOD%C5%BDA_druh%C3%A1_m%C3%ADza_crop.jpg/255px-HOD%C5%BDA_druh%C3%A1_m%C3%ADza_crop.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/fa/HOD%C5%BDA_druh%C3%A1_m%C3%ADza_crop.jpg 2x" data-file-width="305" data-file-height="410" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Enver_Hoxha" title="Enver Hoxha">Enver Hoxha</a> served as <a href="/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Albania" title="Prime Minister of Albania">Prime Minister</a> and <a href="/wiki/Secretary_(title)#Secretary-General" title="Secretary (title)">First Secretary</a> of the <a href="/wiki/Party_of_Labour_of_Albania" title="Party of Labour of Albania">Party of Labour of Albania</a>.</figcaption></figure>
<p>In the aftermath of World War II and the defeat of the <a href="/wiki/Axis_powers" title="Axis powers">Axis Powers</a>, the country became initially a <a href="/wiki/Soviet_satellite" class="mw-redirect" title="Soviet satellite">satellite state</a> of the <a href="/wiki/Soviet_Union" title="Soviet Union">Soviet Union</a>, and Enver Hoxha emerged as the leader of the newly established <a href="/wiki/People%27s_Socialist_Republic_of_Albania" title="People&#39;s Socialist Republic of Albania">People's Republic of Albania</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-97" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-97">&#91;95&#93;</a></sup> Soviet-Albanian relations <a href="/wiki/Soviet%E2%80%93Albanian_split" class="mw-redirect" title="Soviet–Albanian split">began to deteriorate</a> after Stalin's death in 1953. At this point, the country started to develop foreign relations with other communist countries, among others with the <a href="/wiki/People%27s_Republic_of_China" class="mw-redirect" title="People&#39;s Republic of China">People's Republic of China</a>.
</p><p>During this period, the country experienced an increasing industrialisation and urbanisation, a rapid collectivisation and economic growth which led to a higher standard of living.<sup id="cite_ref-Albanian_Nationalism_96-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Albanian_Nationalism-96">&#91;94&#93;</a></sup> The government called for the development of infrastructure and most notably the introduction of a <a href="/wiki/Hekurudha_Shqiptare" title="Hekurudha Shqiptare">railway system</a> that completely revamped transportation. The new land reform laws were passed granting ownership of the land to the workers and peasants who tilled it. Agriculture became <a href="/wiki/Worker_cooperative" title="Worker cooperative">cooperative</a>, and production increased significantly, leading to the country becoming agriculturally self-sufficient. In the field of education, illiteracy was eliminated among the country's adult population.<sup id="cite_ref-98" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-98">&#91;96&#93;</a></sup> The government also oversaw the emancipation of women and the expansion of healthcare and education throughout the country.<sup id="cite_ref-99" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-99">&#91;97&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The average annual increase in the country's national income was 29% and 56% higher than the world and European average, respectively.<sup id="cite_ref-100" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-100">&#91;98&#93;</a></sup><sup class="noprint Inline-Template" style="white-space:nowrap;">&#91;<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability" title="Wikipedia:Verifiability"><span title="The material near this tag failed verification of its source citation(s). (November 2016)">failed verification</span></a></i>&#93;</sup> The nation incurred large debts initially with Yugoslavia until 1948, then the Soviet Union until 1961 and China from the middle of the 1950s.<sup id="cite_ref-101" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-101">&#91;99&#93;</a></sup> The constitution of the communist regime did not allow taxes on individuals, instead, taxes were imposed on cooperatives and other organisations, with much the same effect.<sup id="cite_ref-102" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-102">&#91;100&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Bunker_in_Albanian_Alps.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0c/Bunker_in_Albanian_Alps.jpg/220px-Bunker_in_Albanian_Alps.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="176" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0c/Bunker_in_Albanian_Alps.jpg/330px-Bunker_in_Albanian_Alps.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0c/Bunker_in_Albanian_Alps.jpg/440px-Bunker_in_Albanian_Alps.jpg 2x" data-file-width="984" data-file-height="786" /></a><figcaption>A <a href="/wiki/Bunkers_in_Albania" title="Bunkers in Albania">bunker</a> overlooking the <a href="/wiki/Prokletije" class="mw-redirect" title="Prokletije">Albanian Alps</a>. By 1983, approximately 173,371 concrete bunkers were scattered across the country.<sup id="cite_ref-103" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-103">&#91;101&#93;</a></sup></figcaption></figure>
<p>Today a <a href="/wiki/Secular_state" title="Secular state">secular state</a> without any <a href="/wiki/Official_religion" class="mw-redirect" title="Official religion">official religion</a>, <a href="/wiki/Freedom_of_religion_in_Albania" title="Freedom of religion in Albania">religious freedoms</a> and practises were severely curtailed during the communist era with all forms of worship being outlawed.
