In 1945, the Agrarian Reform Law meant that large swaths of property owned by religious groups were nationalised, mostly the <a href="/wiki/Waqfs" class="mw-redirect" title="Waqfs">waqfs</a> along with the estates of mosques, tekkes, monasteries and dioceses. Many believers, along with the <a href="/wiki/Ulema" class="mw-redirect" title="Ulema">ulema</a> and many priests, were arrested and executed. In 1949, a new Decree on Religious Communities required that all their activities be sanctioned by the state alone.<sup id="cite_ref-104" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-104">&#91;102&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>After hundreds of mosques and dozens of Islamic libraries containing priceless manuscripts were destroyed, Hoxha proclaimed Albania the world's first <a href="/wiki/State_atheism" title="State atheism">atheist state</a> in 1967.<sup id="cite_ref-105" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-105">&#91;103&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Elsie_p27_106-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Elsie_p27-106">&#91;104&#93;</a></sup> The churches had not been spared either and many were converted into cultural centres for young people. A 1967 law banned all fascist, religious, and antisocialist activity and propaganda. The anti-religious policy of Hoxha attained its most fundamental legal and political expression a decade later: "The state recognises no religion", states the 1976 constitution, "and supports and carries out atheistic propaganda in order to implant a scientific materialistic world outlook in people".<sup id="cite_ref-Elsie_p27_106-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Elsie_p27-106">&#91;104&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Fourth_Republic">Fourth Republic</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Fall_of_communism_in_Albania" title="Fall of communism in Albania">Fall of communism in Albania</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Further information: <a href="/wiki/Pyramid_schemes_in_Albania" title="Pyramid schemes in Albania">Pyramid schemes</a> and <a href="/wiki/Albanian_civil_war_of_1997" class="mw-redirect" title="Albanian civil war of 1997">civil war of 1997</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Tirana_Square_1988.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cf/Tirana_Square_1988.jpg/220px-Tirana_Square_1988.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="143" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cf/Tirana_Square_1988.jpg/330px-Tirana_Square_1988.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cf/Tirana_Square_1988.jpg/440px-Tirana_Square_1988.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1581" data-file-height="1025" /></a><figcaption>In 1988, the first foreigners were allowed to walk into the car-free <a href="/wiki/Skanderbeg_Square" title="Skanderbeg Square">Skanderbeg Square</a> in <a href="/wiki/Tirana" title="Tirana">Tirana</a>.</figcaption></figure>
<p>After enduring four decades of communism paired with the <a href="/wiki/Revolutions_of_1989" title="Revolutions of 1989">revolutions of 1989</a>, Albania witnessed a notable rise in political activism, particularly among the students, which ultimately lead to a transformation in the prevailing order. Subsequent to the attainment of widespread in the first <a href="/wiki/Multi-party_elections" class="mw-redirect" title="Multi-party elections">multi-party elections</a> of <a href="/wiki/Albanian_parliamentary_election,_1991" class="mw-redirect" title="Albanian parliamentary election, 1991">1991</a>, the communist party maintained a stronghold in the parliament until their defeat in the <a href="/wiki/Albanian_parliamentary_election,_1992" class="mw-redirect" title="Albanian parliamentary election, 1992">parliamentary elections of 1992</a> directed by the <a href="/wiki/Democratic_Party_of_Albania" title="Democratic Party of Albania">Democratic Party</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-107" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-107">&#91;105&#93;</a></sup> Considerable economic and financial resources were devoted to <a href="/wiki/Pyramid_schemes_in_Albania" title="Pyramid schemes in Albania">pyramid schemes</a> that were widely supported by the government. The schemes swept up somewhere between one sixth and one third of the population of the country.<sup id="cite_ref-108" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-108">&#91;106&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-109" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-109">&#91;107&#93;</a></sup> Despite the warnings of the <a href="/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund" title="International Monetary Fund">International Monetary Fund</a>, <a href="/wiki/Sali_Berisha" title="Sali Berisha">Sali Berisha</a> defended the schemes as large investment firms, leading more people to redirect their remittances and sell their homes and cattle for cash to deposit in the schemes.<sup id="cite_ref-110" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-110">&#91;108&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The schemes began to collapse in late 1996, leading many of the investors to join initially peaceful protests against the government, requesting their money back. The protests turned violent in February 1997 as government forces responded by firing on the demonstrators. In March, the Police and Republican Guard deserted, leaving their armouries open. These were promptly emptied by militias and criminal gangs. The resulting <a href="/wiki/Albanian_Civil_War" class="mw-redirect" title="Albanian Civil War">civil war</a> caused a wave of evacuations of foreign nationals and refugees.<sup id="cite_ref-111" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-111">&#91;109&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The crisis led both <a href="/wiki/Aleksand%C3%ABr_Meksi" title="Aleksandër Meksi">Aleksandër Meksi</a> and <a href="/wiki/Sali_Berisha" title="Sali Berisha">Sali Berisha</a> to resign from office in the wake of the general election. In April 1997, <a href="/wiki/Operation_Alba" title="Operation Alba">Operation Alba</a>, a UN peacekeeping force led by Italy, entered the country with two goals exclusively to assist with the evacuation of expatriates and to secure the ground for international organisations. The main international organisation that was involved was the <a href="/wiki/Western_European_Union" title="Western European Union">Western European Union</a>'s <a href="/wiki/Albanian_civil_war_of_1997#International_intervention" class="mw-redirect" title="Albanian civil war of 1997">multinational</a> <a href="/wiki/Albanian_Police" class="mw-redirect" title="Albanian Police">Albanian Police</a> element, which worked with the government to restructure the <a href="/wiki/Judicial_system_of_Albania" class="mw-redirect" title="Judicial system of Albania">judicial system</a> and simultaneously the Albanian police.
</p>
<div style="clear:both;"></div>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Contemporary">Contemporary</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/Accession_of_Albania_to_the_European_Union" title="Accession of Albania to the European Union">Accession of Albania to the EU</a> and <a href="/wiki/Albania%E2%80%93NATO_relations" title="Albania–NATO relations">NATO</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Further information: <a href="/wiki/2019_Albania_earthquake" title="2019 Albania earthquake">2019 Albania earthquake</a> and <a href="/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Albania" title="COVID-19 pandemic in Albania">COVID-19 pandemic in Albania</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:2019-11-26_Mamurras,_Albania_M6.4_earthquake_shakemap_(USGS).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/49/2019-11-26_Mamurras%2C_Albania_M6.4_earthquake_shakemap_%28USGS%29.jpg/220px-2019-11-26_Mamurras%2C_Albania_M6.4_earthquake_shakemap_%28USGS%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="280" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/49/2019-11-26_Mamurras%2C_Albania_M6.4_earthquake_shakemap_%28USGS%29.jpg/330px-2019-11-26_Mamurras%2C_Albania_M6.4_earthquake_shakemap_%28USGS%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/49/2019-11-26_Mamurras%2C_Albania_M6.4_earthquake_shakemap_%28USGS%29.jpg/440px-2019-11-26_Mamurras%2C_Albania_M6.4_earthquake_shakemap_%28USGS%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="786" data-file-height="1001" /></a><figcaption>The <a href="/wiki/2019_Albania_earthquake" title="2019 Albania earthquake">earthquake of November 2019</a> was the strongest to hit Albania in more than four decades.<sup id="cite_ref-112" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-112">&#91;110&#93;</a></sup></figcaption></figure>
<p>Following the disintegration of the <a href="/wiki/Communist_Albania" class="mw-redirect" title="Communist Albania">communist system</a>, Albania embarked on an active path towards <a href="/wiki/Westernisation" class="mw-redirect" title="Westernisation">Westernisation</a> with the ambition to obtain membership in the <a href="/wiki/European_Union" title="European Union">European Union</a> (EU) and the <a href="/wiki/North_Atlantic_Treaty_Organization" class="mw-redirect" title="North Atlantic Treaty Organization">North Atlantic Treaty Organization</a> (NATO).<sup id="cite_ref-113" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-113">&#91;111&#93;</a></sup> A notable milestone was reached in 2009 when the country attained <a href="/wiki/Albania%E2%80%93NATO_relations" title="Albania–NATO relations">membership</a> in NATO, marking a pioneering achievement among the nations of <a href="/wiki/Southeast_Europe" title="Southeast Europe">Southeast Europe</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-114" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-114">&#91;112&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-115" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-115">&#91;113&#93;</a></sup> In adherence to its vision for further integration into the EU, it <a href="/wiki/Accession_of_Albania_to_the_European_Union" title="Accession of Albania to the European Union">formally applied</a> for membership on 28 April 2009.<sup id="cite_ref-116" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-116">&#91;114&#93;</a></sup> Another milestone was reached on 24 June 2014, when the country was granted <a href="/wiki/Future_enlargement_of_the_European_Union" class="mw-redirect" title="Future enlargement of the European Union">official candidate status</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-EU_CS_117-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-EU_CS-117">&#91;115&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p><a href="/wiki/Edi_Rama" title="Edi Rama">Edi Rama</a> of the <a href="/wiki/Socialist_Party_of_Albania" title="Socialist Party of Albania">Socialist Party</a> won both the <a href="/wiki/Albanian_parliamentary_election,_2013" class="mw-redirect" title="Albanian parliamentary election, 2013">2013</a> and <a href="/wiki/Albanian_parliamentary_election,_2017" class="mw-redirect" title="Albanian parliamentary election, 2017">2017 parliamentary elections</a>. As <a href="/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Albania" title="Prime Minister of Albania">Prime Minister</a>, he implemented numerous reforms focused on <a href="/wiki/Modernism" title="Modernism">modernising</a> the <a href="/wiki/Economy_of_Albania" title="Economy of Albania">economy</a>, as well as democratising state institutions, including the country's <a href="/wiki/Judiciary_of_Albania" title="Judiciary of Albania">judiciary</a> and <a href="/wiki/Law_enforcement_in_Albania" title="Law enforcement in Albania">law enforcement</a>. Unemployment has been steadily reduced, with Albania achieving the 4th lowest <a href="/wiki/List_of_countries_by_unemployment_rate" title="List of countries by unemployment rate">unemployment rate</a> in the Balkans.<sup id="cite_ref-118" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-118">&#91;116&#93;</a></sup> Rama has also placed <a href="/wiki/Gender_equality" title="Gender equality">gender equality</a> at the centre of his agenda; since 2017 almost 50% of the ministers are female, the largest number of women serving in the country's history.<sup id="cite_ref-119" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-119">&#91;117&#93;</a></sup> During the <a href="/wiki/2021_Albanian_parliamentary_election" title="2021 Albanian parliamentary election">2021 parliamentary elections</a>, the ruling Socialist Party led by Edi Rama secured its third consecutive victory, winning nearly half of votes and enough seats in parliament to govern alone.<sup id="cite_ref-120" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-120">&#91;118&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-121" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-121">&#91;119&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>On 26 November 2019, a 6.4 <a href="/wiki/Moment_magnitude_scale" title="Moment magnitude scale">magnitude</a> <a href="/wiki/Earthquake" title="Earthquake">earthquake</a> ravaged Albania with the <a href="/wiki/Epicentre" class="mw-redirect" title="Epicentre">epicentre</a> positioned approximately 16&#160;km (10&#160;mi) southwest of the town of <a href="/wiki/Mamurras" title="Mamurras">Mamurras</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-122" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-122">&#91;120&#93;</a></sup> The tremor was felt in <a href="/wiki/Tirana" title="Tirana">Tirana</a> and in places as far away as <a href="/wiki/Taranto" title="Taranto">Taranto</a>, Italy, and <a href="/wiki/Belgrade" title="Belgrade">Belgrade</a>, Serbia, while the most affected areas were the coastal city of <a href="/wiki/Durr%C3%ABs" title="Durrës">Durrës</a> and the village of <a href="/wiki/Kod%C3%ABr-Thuman%C3%AB" title="Kodër-Thumanë">Kodër-Thumanë</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-123" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-123">&#91;121&#93;</a></sup> Comprehensive response to the earthquake included substantial humanitarian aid from the <a href="/wiki/Albanian_diaspora" title="Albanian diaspora">Albanian diaspora</a> and various countries <a href="/wiki/2019_Albania_earthquake#International_assistance" title="2019 Albania earthquake">around the world</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-124" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-124">&#91;122&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>On 9 March 2020, <a href="/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Albania" title="COVID-19 pandemic in Albania">COVID-19</a> was confirmed to have spread to Albania.<sup id="cite_ref-125" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-125">&#91;123&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-126" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-126">&#91;124&#93;</a></sup> From March to June 2020, the government declared a <a href="/wiki/State_of_emergency" title="State of emergency">state of emergency</a> as a measure to limit the rapid spread of the pandemic in the country.<sup id="cite_ref-127" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-127">&#91;125&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-128" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-128">&#91;126&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-129" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-129">&#91;127&#93;</a></sup> The country's COVID-19 <a href="/wiki/COVID-19_vaccination_in_Albania" title="COVID-19 vaccination in Albania">vaccination campaign</a> started on 11 January 2021, however, as of 11 August 2021, the total number of vaccines administered so far in Albania amounts to 1,280,239 doses.<sup id="cite_ref-130" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-130">&#91;128&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-131" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-131">&#91;129&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Environment">Environment</span></h2>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Geography">Geography</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Geography_of_Albania" title="Geography of Albania">Geography of Albania</a></div>
<figure class="mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Valbona_nga_Kukaj.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0f/Valbona_nga_Kukaj.jpg/300px-Valbona_nga_Kukaj.jpg" decoding="async" width="300" height="110" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0f/Valbona_nga_Kukaj.jpg/450px-Valbona_nga_Kukaj.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0f/Valbona_nga_Kukaj.jpg/600px-Valbona_nga_Kukaj.jpg 2x" data-file-width="6460" data-file-height="2377" /></a><figcaption>The <a href="/wiki/Albanian_Alps" class="mw-redirect" title="Albanian Alps">Albanian Alps</a> are an extension and simultaneously the highest section of the <a href="/wiki/Dinaric_Alps" title="Dinaric Alps">Dinaric Alps</a>.</figcaption></figure>
<p>With an area of 28,748&#160;km<sup>2</sup> (11,100&#160;sq&#160;mi), Albania is situated along the <a href="/wiki/Mediterranean_Sea" title="Mediterranean Sea">Mediterranean Sea</a> on the <a href="/wiki/Balkan_Peninsula" class="mw-redirect" title="Balkan Peninsula">Balkan Peninsula</a> in <a href="/wiki/Southern_Europe" title="Southern Europe">South</a> and <a href="/wiki/Southeast_Europe" title="Southeast Europe">Southeast Europe</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Albania_pdf_132-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Albania_pdf-132">&#91;130&#93;</a></sup> The country is bordered by the <a href="/wiki/Adriatic_Sea" title="Adriatic Sea">Adriatic Sea</a> to the west, <a href="/wiki/Montenegro" title="Montenegro">Montenegro</a> to the northwest, <a href="/wiki/Kosovo" title="Kosovo">Kosovo</a> to the northeast, <a href="/wiki/North_Macedonia" title="North Macedonia">North Macedonia</a> to the east, <a href="/wiki/Greece" title="Greece">Greece</a> to the south and the <a href="/wiki/Ionian_Sea" title="Ionian Sea">Ionian Sea</a> to the southwest. It is positioned between latitudes <a href="/wiki/42nd_parallel_north" title="42nd parallel north">42°</a> and <a href="/wiki/39th_parallel_north" title="39th parallel north">39° N</a>, and longitudes <a href="/wiki/21st_meridian_east" title="21st meridian east">21°</a> and <a href="/wiki/19th_meridian_east" title="19th meridian east">19° E</a>. Geographic coordinates include <a href="/wiki/V%C3%ABrmosh" class="mw-redirect" title="Vërmosh">Vërmosh</a> at 42° 35' 34" northern latitude as the northernmost point, <a href="/wiki/Konispol" title="Konispol">Konispol</a> at 39° 40' 0" northern latitude as the southernmost point, <a href="/wiki/Sazan_Island" class="mw-redirect" title="Sazan Island">Sazan</a> at 19° 16' 50" eastern longitude as the westernmost point and <a href="/wiki/V%C3%ABrnik" class="mw-redirect" title="Vërnik">Vërnik</a> at 21° 1' 26" eastern longitude as the easternmost point.<sup id="cite_ref-133" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-133">&#91;131&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Mount_Korab" class="mw-redirect" title="Mount Korab">Mount Korab</a>, rising at 2,764&#160;m (9,068.24&#160;ft) <a href="/wiki/Metres_above_the_Adriatic" title="Metres above the Adriatic">above the Adriatic</a>, is the highest point, while the Mediterranean Sea, at 0&#160;m (0.00&#160;ft), is the lowest point. The country extends 148&#160;km (92&#160;mi) from east to west and around 340&#160;km (211&#160;mi) from north to south.
</p><p>Albania possesses a diverse and varied landscape with mountains and hills that traverse its territory in various directions. The country is home to extensive mountain ranges, including the <a href="/wiki/Albanian_Alps" class="mw-redirect" title="Albanian Alps">Albanian Alps</a> in the north, the <a href="/wiki/Korab" title="Korab">Korab Mountains</a> in the east, the <a href="/wiki/Pindus_Mountains" class="mw-redirect" title="Pindus Mountains">Pindus Mountains</a> in the southeast, the <a href="/wiki/Ceraunian_Mountains" title="Ceraunian Mountains">Ceraunian Mountains</a> in the southwest and the <a href="/wiki/Skanderbeg_Mountains" title="Skanderbeg Mountains">Skanderbeg Mountains</a> in the centre. In the northwest, the country boasts the remarkable <a href="/wiki/Lake_of_Shkod%C3%ABr" class="mw-redirect" title="Lake of Shkodër">Lake of Shkodër</a>, recognised as the largest lake in Southern Europe.<sup id="cite_ref-134" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-134">&#91;132&#93;</a></sup> Towards the <a href="/wiki/Albanian_Ohrid_Lake_Coast" class="mw-redirect" title="Albanian Ohrid Lake Coast">southeast</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Lake_of_Ohrid" class="mw-redirect" title="Lake of Ohrid">Lake of Ohrid</a> emerges, renowned as one of the world's oldest continuously existing lakes.<sup id="cite_ref-135" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-135">&#91;133&#93;</a></sup> Further to the south, the expanse includes the <a href="/wiki/Prespa_Lake" class="mw-redirect" title="Prespa Lake">Large</a> and <a href="/wiki/Small_Prespa_Lake" title="Small Prespa Lake">Small Lake of Prespa</a>, distinguished as some of the highest positioned lakes in the Balkans. Rivers rise mostly in the east of Albania and discharge into the Adriatic Sea but as well as into the Ionian Sea to a lesser extent. The longest river in the country, measured from its mouth to its source, is the <a href="/wiki/Drin_River" class="mw-redirect" title="Drin River">Drin</a> that starts at the confluence of its two headwaters, the <a href="/wiki/Black_Drin" title="Black Drin">Black</a> and <a href="/wiki/White_Drin" title="White Drin">White Drin</a>. Of particular concern is the <a href="/wiki/Vjos%C3%AB" class="mw-redirect" title="Vjosë">Vjosë</a>, which represents one of the last intact large river systems in Europe.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Climate">Climate</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Climate_of_Albania" title="Climate of Albania">Climate of Albania</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Gjipe_beach,_Albania.JPG" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/11/Gjipe_beach%2C_Albania.JPG/220px-Gjipe_beach%2C_Albania.JPG" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/11/Gjipe_beach%2C_Albania.JPG/330px-Gjipe_beach%2C_Albania.JPG 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/11/Gjipe_beach%2C_Albania.JPG/440px-Gjipe_beach%2C_Albania.JPG 2x" data-file-width="2304" data-file-height="1536" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Gjipe" class="mw-redirect" title="Gjipe">Gjipe</a> is located on the confluence of the <a href="/wiki/Adriatic_Sea" title="Adriatic Sea">Adriatic</a> and <a href="/wiki/Ionian_Sea" title="Ionian Sea">Ionian Sea</a>, on the <a href="/wiki/Albanian_Riviera" title="Albanian Riviera">Albanian Riviera</a>.</figcaption></figure>
<p>The <a href="/wiki/Climate_of_Albania" title="Climate of Albania">climate of Albania</a> exhibits a distinguished level of variability and diversity due to the differences in latitude, longitude and altitude.<sup id="cite_ref-climate_136-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-climate-136">&#91;134&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-climate2_137-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-climate2-137">&#91;135&#93;</a></sup> Albania experiences a <a href="/wiki/Mediterranean_climate" title="Mediterranean climate">Mediterranean</a> and <a href="/wiki/Continental_climate" title="Continental climate">Continental climate</a>, characterised by the presence of four distinct seasons.<sup id="cite_ref-climate1_138-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-climate1-138">&#91;136&#93;</a></sup> According to the <a href="/wiki/K%C3%B6ppen_climate_classification" title="Köppen climate classification">Köppen classification</a>, Albania encompasses five primary climatic types, spanning from Mediterranean and <a href="/wiki/Humid_subtropical_climate" title="Humid subtropical climate">subtropical</a> in the western half to <a href="/wiki/Oceanic_climate" title="Oceanic climate">oceanic</a>, <a href="/wiki/Humid_continental_climate" title="Humid continental climate">continental</a> and <a href="/wiki/Subarctic_climate" title="Subarctic climate">subarctic</a> in the eastern half of the country.<sup id="cite_ref-139" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-139">&#91;137&#93;</a></sup> The coastal regions along the <a href="/wiki/Albanian_Adriatic_Sea_Coast" title="Albanian Adriatic Sea Coast">Adriatic</a> and <a href="/wiki/Albanian_Ionian_Sea_Coast" title="Albanian Ionian Sea Coast">Ionian Seas</a> in Albania are acknowledged as the warmest areas, while the northern and eastern regions encompassing the <a href="/wiki/Albanian_Alps" class="mw-redirect" title="Albanian Alps">Albanian Alps</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Korab_Mountains" class="mw-redirect" title="Korab Mountains">Korab Mountains</a> are recognised as the coldest areas in the country.<sup id="cite_ref-climate3_140-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-climate3-140">&#91;138&#93;</a></sup> Throughout the year, the average monthly temperatures fluctuate, ranging from −1&#160;<a href="/wiki/Celsius" title="Celsius">°C</a> (30&#160;<a href="/wiki/Fahrenheit" title="Fahrenheit">°F</a>) during the winter months to 21.8&#160;°C (71.2&#160;°F) in the summer months. Notably, the highest recorded temperature of 43.9&#160;°C (111.0&#160;°F) was observed in <a href="/wiki/Ku%C3%A7ov%C3%AB" title="Kuçovë">Kuçovë</a> on 18 July 1973, while the lowest temperature of −29&#160;°C (−20&#160;°F) was recorded in Shtyllë, <a href="/wiki/Librazhd" title="Librazhd">Librazhd</a> on 9 January 2017.<sup id="cite_ref-141" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-141">&#91;139&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-142" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-142">&#91;140&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Albania receives most of the <a href="/wiki/Precipitation_(meteorology)" class="mw-redirect" title="Precipitation (meteorology)">precipitation</a> in winter months and less in summer months.<sup id="cite_ref-climate2_137-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-climate2-137">&#91;135&#93;</a></sup> The average precipitation is about 1,485 millimetres (58.5 inches).<sup id="cite_ref-climate3_140-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-climate3-140">&#91;138&#93;</a></sup> The mean annual precipitation ranges between 600 millimetres (24 inches) and 3,000 millimetres (120 inches) depending on geographical location.<sup id="cite_ref-climate1_138-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-climate1-138">&#91;136&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Northern_Mountain_Range_(Albania)" class="mw-redirect" title="Northern Mountain Range (Albania)">northwestern</a> and <a href="/wiki/Southern_Mountain_Range_(Albania)" class="mw-redirect" title="Southern Mountain Range (Albania)">southeastern highlands</a> receive the intenser amount of precipitation, whilst the <a href="/wiki/Northern_Mountain_Range_(Albania)" class="mw-redirect" title="Northern Mountain Range (Albania)">northeastern</a> and <a href="/wiki/Southern_Mountain_Range_(Albania)" class="mw-redirect" title="Southern Mountain Range (Albania)">southwestern highlands</a> as well as the <a href="/wiki/Western_Lowlands" class="mw-redirect" title="Western Lowlands">Western Lowlands</a> the more limited amount.<sup id="cite_ref-climate3_140-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-climate3-140">&#91;138&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Albanian_Alps" class="mw-redirect" title="Albanian Alps">Albanian Alps</a> in the far north of the country are considered to be among the most humid regions of Europe, receiving at least 3,100&#160;mm (122.0&#160;in) of rain annually.<sup id="cite_ref-climate3_140-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-climate3-140">&#91;138&#93;</a></sup> Four <a href="/wiki/Glacier" title="Glacier">glaciers</a> within these mountains were discovered at a relatively low altitude of 2,000 metres (6,600&#160;ft), which is extremely rare for such a southerly latitude.<sup id="cite_ref-143" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-143">&#91;141&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Environmental_issues">Environmental issues</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Environmental_issues_in_Albania" title="Environmental issues in Albania">Environmental issues in Albania</a></div>
<p>Environmental issues in Albania notably encompass <a href="/wiki/Air_pollution" title="Air pollution">air</a> and <a href="/wiki/Water_pollution" title="Water pollution">water pollution</a>, <a href="/wiki/Climate_change_in_Albania" class="mw-redirect" title="Climate change in Albania">climate change</a> impacts, <a href="/wiki/Waste_management" title="Waste management">waste management</a> shortcomings, <a href="/wiki/Conservation_biology" title="Conservation biology">biodiversity loss</a> and imperative for <a href="/wiki/Nature_conservation" title="Nature conservation">nature conservation</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-144" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-144">&#91;142&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-145" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-145">&#91;143&#93;</a></sup> Climate change is predicted to exert significant impacts on the quality of life in Albania.<sup id="cite_ref-146" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-146">&#91;144&#93;</a></sup> The country is recognised as <a href="/wiki/Climate_change_vulnerability" title="Climate change vulnerability">vulnerable to climate change</a> impacts, ranked 79 among 181 countries in the <a href="/wiki/Notre_Dame_Global_Adaptation_Index" title="Notre Dame Global Adaptation Index">Notre Dame Global Adaptation Index</a> of 2020.<sup id="cite_ref-147" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-147">&#91;145&#93;</a></sup> Factors that account for the country's vulnerability to climate change risks include geological and hydrological <a href="/wiki/Hazard" title="Hazard">hazards</a>, including earthquakes, flooding, fires, landslides, torrential rains, river and coastal erosion.<sup id="cite_ref-148" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-148">&#91;146&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-149" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-149">&#91;147&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>As a party to the <a href="/wiki/Kyoto_Protocol" title="Kyoto Protocol">Kyoto Protocol</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Paris_Agreement" title="Paris Agreement">Paris Agreement</a>, Albania is committed to reduce <a href="/wiki/Greenhouse_gas_emissions" title="Greenhouse gas emissions">greenhouse gas emissions</a> by 45% and achieve <a href="/wiki/Carbon_neutrality" class="mw-redirect" title="Carbon neutrality">carbon neutrality</a> by 2050 which, along with national policies, will help to mitigate the impacts of the climate change.<sup id="cite_ref-150" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-150">&#91;148&#93;</a></sup> The country has a moderate and improving performance in the <a href="/wiki/Environmental_Performance_Index" title="Environmental Performance Index">Environmental Performance Index</a> with an overall ranking of 62 out of 180 countries in 2022.<sup id="cite_ref-151" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-151">&#91;149&#93;</a></sup>
Albania's ranking has, however, decreased since its highest placement at position 15 in the Environmental Performance Index of 2012.<sup id="cite_ref-152" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-152">&#91;150&#93;</a></sup> In 2019, Albania had a <a href="/wiki/Forest_Landscape_Integrity_Index" title="Forest Landscape Integrity Index">Forest Landscape Integrity Index</a> mean score of 6.77 from 10, ranking it 64th globally out of 172 countries.<sup id="cite_ref-FLII-Supplementary_153-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FLII-Supplementary-153">&#91;151&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<div class="thumb tnone" style="margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;overflow:hidden;width:auto;max-width:1024px"><div class="thumbinner"><div class="noresize" style="overflow:auto"><span typeof="mw:File"><a href="/wiki/File:Prespa_and_Prespa_National_Park_Albania_2017.jpg" class="mw-file-description" title="The Prespa National Park in southeastern Albania is part of the European Green Belt and Ohrid-Prespa Biosphere Reserve."><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/02/Prespa_and_Prespa_National_Park_Albania_2017.jpg/1016px-Prespa_and_Prespa_National_Park_Albania_2017.jpg" decoding="async" width="1016" height="210" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/02/Prespa_and_Prespa_National_Park_Albania_2017.jpg/1524px-Prespa_and_Prespa_National_Park_Albania_2017.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/02/Prespa_and_Prespa_National_Park_Albania_2017.jpg/2032px-Prespa_and_Prespa_National_Park_Albania_2017.jpg 2x" data-file-width="12331" data-file-height="2548" /></a></span></div><div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Prespa_and_Prespa_National_Park_Albania_2017.jpg" title="File:Prespa and Prespa National Park Albania 2017.jpg"> </a></div><div class="center" style="width:auto; margin-left:auto; margin-right:auto;">The <a href="/wiki/Prespa_National_Park_(Albania)" title="Prespa National Park (Albania)">Prespa National Park</a> in southeastern Albania is part of the <a href="/wiki/European_Green_Belt" title="European Green Belt">European Green Belt</a> and <a href="/wiki/Ohrid-Prespa_Transboundary_Biosphere_Reserve" title="Ohrid-Prespa Transboundary Biosphere Reserve">Ohrid-Prespa Biosphere Reserve</a>.</div></div></div></div>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Conservation">Conservation</span></h2>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Ksamill-1.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0e/Ksamill-1.jpg/220px-Ksamill-1.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0e/Ksamill-1.jpg/330px-Ksamill-1.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0e/Ksamill-1.jpg/440px-Ksamill-1.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1113" data-file-height="742" /></a><figcaption>The <a href="/wiki/Islets_of_Ksamil" title="Islets of Ksamil">islets of Ksamil</a> lie in the <a href="/wiki/Butrint_National_Park" title="Butrint National Park">Butrint National Park</a>.</figcaption></figure>
<p>Albania has been an active participant in numerous international agreements and conventions aimed at strengthing its commitment to the preservation and sustainable management of biological diversity. Since 1994, the country is a party to the <a href="/wiki/Convention_on_Biological_Diversity" title="Convention on Biological Diversity">Convention on Biological Diversity</a> (CBD) and its associated <a href="/wiki/Cartagena_Protocol_on_Biosafety" title="Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety">Cartagena</a> and <a href="/wiki/Nagoya_Protocol" title="Nagoya Protocol">Nagoya Protocols</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-CBD_154-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-CBD-154">&#91;152&#93;</a></sup> To uphold these commitments, it has developed and implemented a comprehensive <a href="/wiki/Biodiversity_action_plan" title="Biodiversity action plan">National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan</a> (NBSAP).<sup id="cite_ref-CBD_154-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-CBD-154">&#91;152&#93;</a></sup> Furthermore, Albania has established a partnership with the <a href="/wiki/International_Union_for_Conservation_of_Nature" title="International Union for Conservation of Nature">International Union for Conservation of Nature</a> (IUCN), advancing its conservation efforts on both national and international scales. Guided by the IUCN, the country has made substantial progress in the foundation of <a href="/wiki/Protected_area" title="Protected area">protected areas</a> within its boundaries, encompassing 12 <a href="/wiki/National_park" title="National park">national parks</a> such as <a href="/wiki/Butrint_National_Park" title="Butrint National Park">Butrint</a>, <a href="/wiki/Karaburun-Sazan_Marine_Park" title="Karaburun-Sazan Marine Park">Karaburun-Sazan</a>, <a href="/wiki/Llogara_National_Park" title="Llogara National Park">Llogara</a>, <a href="/wiki/Prespa_National_Park_(Albania)" title="Prespa National Park (Albania)">Prespa</a> and <a href="/wiki/Vjosa_Wild_River_National_Park" title="Vjosa Wild River National Park">Vjosa</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-New_NP_155-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-New_NP-155">&#91;153&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>As a signatory to the <a href="/wiki/Ramsar_Convention" title="Ramsar Convention">Ramsar Convention</a>, Albania has granted special recognition upon four wetlands, designating them as Wetlands of International Importance, including <a href="/wiki/Bojana_(river)" title="Bojana (river)">Buna</a>-<a href="/wiki/Lake_Skadar" title="Lake Skadar">Shkodër</a>, <a href="/wiki/Butrint_Lagoon" title="Butrint Lagoon">Butrint</a>, <a href="/wiki/Karavasta_Lagoon" title="Karavasta Lagoon">Karavasta</a> and <a href="/wiki/Lake_Prespa" title="Lake Prespa">Prespa</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-156" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-156">&#91;154&#93;</a></sup> The country's dedication to protection extends further into the sphere of <a href="/wiki/UNESCO" title="UNESCO">UNESCO</a>'s <a href="/wiki/World_Network_of_Biosphere_Reserves" title="World Network of Biosphere Reserves">World Network of Biosphere Reserves</a>, operating within the framework of the <a href="/wiki/Man_and_the_Biosphere_Programme" title="Man and the Biosphere Programme">Man and the Biosphere Programme</a>, evidenced by its engagement in the <a href="/wiki/Ohrid-Prespa_Transboundary_Biosphere_Reserve" title="Ohrid-Prespa Transboundary Biosphere Reserve">Ohrid-Prespa Transboundary Biosphere Reserve</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-157" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-157">&#91;155&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-158" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-158">&#91;156&#93;</a></sup> Furthermore, Albania is host to two natural <a href="/wiki/World_Heritage_Site" title="World Heritage Site">World Heritage Sites</a>, which encompass the Ohrid region and both the <a href="/wiki/Gashi_River" class="mw-redirect" title="Gashi River">Gashi River</a> and <a href="/wiki/Rrajce" class="mw-redirect" title="Rrajce">Rrajca</a> as part of <a href="/wiki/Ancient_and_Primeval_Beech_Forests_of_the_Carpathians_and_Other_Regions_of_Europe" title="Ancient and Primeval Beech Forests of the Carpathians and Other Regions of Europe">Ancient and Primeval Beech Forests of the Carpathians and Other Regions of Europe</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Ancient_Primeval_Beech_Forests_159-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Ancient_Primeval_Beech_Forests-159">&#91;157&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Biodiversity">Biodiversity</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Biodiversity_of_Albania" title="Biodiversity of Albania">Biodiversity of Albania</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/List_of_ecoregions_in_Albania" title="List of ecoregions in Albania">Ecoregions in Albania</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Golden_eagle_(13434882845).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5b/Golden_eagle_%2813434882845%29.jpg/220px-Golden_eagle_%2813434882845%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="146" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5b/Golden_eagle_%2813434882845%29.jpg/330px-Golden_eagle_%2813434882845%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5b/Golden_eagle_%2813434882845%29.jpg/440px-Golden_eagle_%2813434882845%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="4928" data-file-height="3280" /></a><figcaption>The <a href="/wiki/Golden_eagle" title="Golden eagle">golden eagle</a> is the national symbol and animal of Albania.</figcaption></figure>
<p>A <a href="/wiki/Biodiversity_hotspot" title="Biodiversity hotspot">biodiversity hotspot</a>, Albania possesses an exceptionally rich and contrasting <a href="/wiki/Biodiversity" title="Biodiversity">biodiversity</a> on account of its geographical location at the centre of the <a href="/wiki/Mediterranean_Sea" title="Mediterranean Sea">Mediterranean Sea</a> and the great diversity in its <a href="/wiki/Climatic" class="mw-redirect" title="Climatic">climatic</a>, geological and <a href="/wiki/Hydrological" class="mw-redirect" title="Hydrological">hydrological</a> conditions.<sup id="cite_ref-160" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-160">&#91;158&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-161" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-161">&#91;159&#93;</a></sup> Because of remoteness, the mountains and hills of Albania are endowed with forests, trees and grasses that are essential to the lives for a wide variety of animals, among others for two of the most <a href="/wiki/Endangered_species" title="Endangered species">endangered species</a> of the country, the <a href="/wiki/Balkan_lynx" title="Balkan lynx">lynx</a> and <a href="/wiki/Brown_bear" title="Brown bear">brown bear</a>, as well as the <a href="/wiki/Wildcat" title="Wildcat">wildcat</a>, <a href="/wiki/Grey_wolf" class="mw-redirect" title="Grey wolf">grey wolf</a>, <a href="/wiki/Red_fox" title="Red fox">red fox</a>, <a href="/wiki/Golden_jackal" title="Golden jackal">golden jackal</a>, <a href="/wiki/Egyptian_vulture" title="Egyptian vulture">Egyptian vulture</a> and <a href="/wiki/Golden_eagle" title="Golden eagle">golden eagle</a>, the latter constituting the national animal of the country.<sup id="cite_ref-162" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-162">&#91;160&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-163" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-163">&#91;161&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-164" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-164">&#91;162&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-165" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-165">&#91;163&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The estuaries, wetlands and lakes are extraordinarily important for the <a href="/wiki/Greater_flamingo" title="Greater flamingo">greater flamingo</a>, <a href="/wiki/Pygmy_cormorant" title="Pygmy cormorant">pygmy cormorant</a> and the extremely rare and perhaps the most iconic bird of the country, the <a href="/wiki/Dalmatian_pelican" title="Dalmatian pelican">dalmatian pelican</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-166" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-166">&#91;164&#93;</a></sup> Of particular importance are the <a href="/wiki/Mediterranean_monk_seal" title="Mediterranean monk seal">Mediterranean monk seal</a>, <a href="/wiki/Loggerhead_sea_turtle" title="Loggerhead sea turtle">loggerhead sea turtle</a> and <a href="/wiki/Green_sea_turtle" title="Green sea turtle">green sea turtle</a> that use to nest on the country's coastal waters and shores.
</p><p>In terms of <a href="/wiki/Phytogeography" title="Phytogeography">phytogeography</a>, Albania is part of the <a href="/wiki/Boreal_Kingdom" title="Boreal Kingdom">Boreal Kingdom</a> and stretches specifically within the <a href="/wiki/Illyria" title="Illyria">Illyrian</a> province of the <a href="/wiki/Circumboreal_Region" title="Circumboreal Region">Circumboreal</a> and <a href="/wiki/Mediterranean_Basin" title="Mediterranean Basin">Mediterranean Region</a>. Its territory can be subdivided into four terrestrial <a href="/wiki/Ecoregion" title="Ecoregion">ecoregions</a> of the <a href="/wiki/Palearctic_realm" title="Palearctic realm">Palearctic realm</a> namely within the <a href="/wiki/Illyrian_deciduous_forests" title="Illyrian deciduous forests">Illyrian deciduous forests</a>, <a href="/wiki/Balkan_mixed_forests" title="Balkan mixed forests">Balkan mixed forests</a>, <a href="/wiki/Pindus_Mountains_mixed_forests" title="Pindus Mountains mixed forests">Pindus Mountains mixed forests</a> and <a href="/wiki/Dinaric_Mountains_mixed_forests" title="Dinaric Mountains mixed forests">Dinaric Mountains mixed forests</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-167" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-167">&#91;165&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-168" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-168">&#91;166&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Approximately 3,500 different species of plants can be found in Albania which refers principally to a <a href="/wiki/Mediterranean" class="mw-redirect" title="Mediterranean">Mediterranean</a> and <a href="/wiki/Eurasia" title="Eurasia">Eurasian</a> character. The country maintains a vibrant tradition of herbal and medicinal practices. At the minimum 300 plants growing locally are used in the preparation of herbs and medicines.<sup id="cite_ref-169" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-169">&#91;167&#93;</a></sup> The trees within the forests are primarily <a href="/wiki/Fir" title="Fir">fir</a>, <a href="/wiki/Oak" title="Oak">oak</a>, <a href="/wiki/Beech" title="Beech">beech</a> and <a href="/wiki/Pine" title="Pine">pine</a>.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Protected_areas">Protected areas</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Protected_areas_of_Albania" title="Protected areas of Albania">Protected areas of Albania</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:A_fishermen_house_in_Karavasta_Lagoon_(Divjak%C3%AB-Karavasta_National_Park).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/42/A_fishermen_house_in_Karavasta_Lagoon_%28Divjak%C3%AB-Karavasta_National_Park%29.jpg/220px-A_fishermen_house_in_Karavasta_Lagoon_%28Divjak%C3%AB-Karavasta_National_Park%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/42/A_fishermen_house_in_Karavasta_Lagoon_%28Divjak%C3%AB-Karavasta_National_Park%29.jpg/330px-A_fishermen_house_in_Karavasta_Lagoon_%28Divjak%C3%AB-Karavasta_National_Park%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/42/A_fishermen_house_in_Karavasta_Lagoon_%28Divjak%C3%AB-Karavasta_National_Park%29.jpg/440px-A_fishermen_house_in_Karavasta_Lagoon_%28Divjak%C3%AB-Karavasta_National_Park%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="5160" data-file-height="3440" /></a><figcaption>The <a href="/wiki/Lagoon_of_Karavasta" class="mw-redirect" title="Lagoon of Karavasta">lagoon of Karavasta</a> within the <a href="/wiki/Divjak%C3%AB-Karavasta_National_Park" title="Divjakë-Karavasta National Park">Divjakë-Karavasta National Park</a>.</figcaption></figure>
<p>The <a href="/wiki/Protected_areas_of_Albania" title="Protected areas of Albania">protected areas of Albania</a> are areas designated and managed by the <a href="/wiki/Albanian_government" class="mw-redirect" title="Albanian government">Albanian government</a>. There are 12 <a href="/wiki/National_park" title="National park">national parks</a>, 4 <a href="/wiki/Ramsar_site" title="Ramsar site">ramsar sites</a>, 1 <a href="/wiki/Biosphere_reserve" class="mw-redirect" title="Biosphere reserve">biosphere reserve</a> and 786 other types of conservation reserves in Albania.<sup id="cite_ref-New_NP_155-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-New_NP-155">&#91;153&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-170" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-170">&#91;168&#93;</a></sup> Located in the north, the Albanian Alps National Park, comprising the former <a href="/wiki/Theth_National_Park" title="Theth National Park">Theth National Park</a> and <a href="/wiki/Valbon%C3%AB_Valley_National_Park" class="mw-redirect" title="Valbonë Valley National Park">Valbonë Valley National Park</a>, is surrounded amidst the towering peaks of the <a href="/wiki/Accursed_Mountains" title="Accursed Mountains">Albanian Alps</a>. In the east, portions of the rugged <a href="/wiki/Korab" title="Korab">Korab</a>, <a href="/wiki/Nem%C3%ABr%C3%A7ka" title="Nemërçka">Nemërçka</a> and <a href="/wiki/Shebenik" title="Shebenik">Shebenik</a> Mountains are conserved within the boundaries of <a href="/wiki/Fir_of_Hotov%C3%AB-Dang%C3%ABlli_National_Park" title="Fir of Hotovë-Dangëlli National Park">Fir of Hotovë-Dangëlli National Park</a>, <a href="/wiki/Shebenik_National_Park" title="Shebenik National Park">Shebenik National Park</a> and <a href="/wiki/Prespa_National_Park_(Albania)" title="Prespa National Park (Albania)">Prespa National Park</a>, with the latter encompassing Albania's share of the <a href="/wiki/Prespa_Lake" class="mw-redirect" title="Prespa Lake">Great</a> and <a href="/wiki/Small_Prespa_Lake" title="Small Prespa Lake">Small Lakes of Prespa</a>.
</p><p>To the south, the <a href="/wiki/Ceraunian_Mountains" title="Ceraunian Mountains">Ceraunian Mountains</a> define the <a href="/wiki/Albanian_Ionian_Sea_Coast" title="Albanian Ionian Sea Coast">Albanian Ionian Sea Coast</a>, shaping the landscape of <a href="/wiki/Llogara_National_Park" title="Llogara National Park">Llogara National Park</a>, which extends into the <a href="/wiki/Karaburun_Peninsula,_Albania" title="Karaburun Peninsula, Albania">Karaburun Peninsula</a>, forming the <a href="/wiki/Karaburun-Sazan_Marine_Park" title="Karaburun-Sazan Marine Park">Karaburun-Sazan Marine Park</a>. Further southward lies <a href="/wiki/Butrint_National_Park" title="Butrint National Park">Butrint National Park</a>, occupying a peninsula surrounded by the Lake of Butrint and the <a href="/wiki/Channel_of_Vivari" title="Channel of Vivari">Channel of Vivari</a>. In the west, stretching along the <a href="/wiki/Albanian_Adriatic_Sea_Coast" title="Albanian Adriatic Sea Coast">Albanian Adriatic Sea Coast</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Divjak%C3%AB-Karavasta_National_Park" title="Divjakë-Karavasta National Park">Divjakë-Karavasta National Park</a> boasts the extensive <a href="/wiki/Lagoon_of_Karavasta" class="mw-redirect" title="Lagoon of Karavasta">Lagoon of Karavasta</a>, one of the largest lagoon systems in the Mediterranean Sea. Notably, Europe's first wild river national park, <a href="/wiki/Vjosa_Wild_River_National_Park" title="Vjosa Wild River National Park">Vjosa National Park</a>, safeguards the <a href="/wiki/Vjosa" title="Vjosa">Vjosa River</a> and its primary tributaries, which originates in the <a href="/wiki/Pindus" title="Pindus">Pindus</a> Mountains and flows to the Adriatic Sea. <a href="/wiki/Dajti_Mountain_National_Park" title="Dajti Mountain National Park">Dajti Mountain National Park</a>, <a href="/wiki/Lur%C3%AB-Dej%C3%AB_Mountain_National_Park" title="Lurë-Dejë Mountain National Park">Lurë-Dejë Mountain National Park</a> and <a href="/wiki/Tomorr_Mountain_National_Park" title="Tomorr Mountain National Park">Tomorr Mountain National Park</a> protect the mountainous terrain of the center of Albania, including the <a href="/wiki/Tomorr" title="Tomorr">Tomorr</a> and <a href="/wiki/Skanderbeg_Mountains" title="Skanderbeg Mountains">Skanderbeg Mountains</a>.
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Governance">Governance</span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Politics_of_Albania" title="Politics of Albania">Politics of Albania</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/Government_of_Albania" class="mw-redirect" title="Government of Albania">Government of Albania</a></div>
<table class="wikitable" style="text-align:left; float:right; margin-right:9px; margin-left:2px;">

<td style="text-align:left;"><span typeof="mw:File"><a href="/wiki/File:Bajram_Begaj_(infobox_crop).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/57/Bajram_Begaj_%28infobox_crop%29.jpg/108px-Bajram_Begaj_%28infobox_crop%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="108" height="150" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/57/Bajram_Begaj_%28infobox_crop%29.jpg/162px-Bajram_Begaj_%28infobox_crop%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/57/Bajram_Begaj_%28infobox_crop%29.jpg/216px-Bajram_Begaj_%28infobox_crop%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="801" data-file-height="1114" /></a></span>

<td style="text-align:center;"><a href="/wiki/Bajram_Begaj" title="Bajram Begaj">Bajram Begaj</a><br /><span style="font-size:85%;"><a href="/wiki/President_of_Albania" title="President of Albania">President</a></span>
</td>
<td style="text-align:center;"><a href="/wiki/Edi_Rama" title="Edi Rama">Edi Rama</a><br /><span style="font-size:85%;"><a href="/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Albania" title="Prime Minister of Albania">Prime Minister</a></span>
</td></tr></tbody></table>
<p>Albania is a <a href="/wiki/Parliamentary_republic" title="Parliamentary republic">parliamentary</a> <a href="/wiki/Constitutional_republic" class="mw-redirect" title="Constitutional republic">constitutional republic</a> and <a href="/wiki/Sovereign_state" title="Sovereign state">sovereign state</a> whose <a href="/wiki/Politics_of_Albania" title="Politics of Albania">politics</a> operate under a framework laid out in the <a href="/wiki/Constitution_of_Albania" title="Constitution of Albania">constitution</a> wherein the <a href="/wiki/President_of_Albania" title="President of Albania">president</a> functions as the <a href="/wiki/Head_of_state" title="Head of state">head of state</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Albania" title="Prime Minister of Albania">prime minister</a> as the <a href="/wiki/Head_of_government" title="Head of government">head of government</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-kushtetuta_171-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-kushtetuta-171">&#91;169&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Sovereignty" title="Sovereignty">sovereignty</a> is vested in the <a href="/wiki/Albanian_people" class="mw-redirect" title="Albanian people">Albanian people</a> and exercised by the Albanian people through their representatives or directly.<sup id="cite_ref-kushtetuta_171-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-kushtetuta-171">&#91;169&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/Government_of_Albania" class="mw-redirect" title="Government of Albania">government</a> is based on the separation and balancing of powers among the <a href="/wiki/Legislative" class="mw-redirect" title="Legislative">legislative</a>, <a href="/wiki/Judiciary" title="Judiciary">judiciary</a> and executive.<sup id="cite_ref-kushtetuta_171-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-kushtetuta-171">&#91;169&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Legislative_power" class="mw-redirect" title="Legislative power">legislative power</a> is held by the <a href="/wiki/Parliament_of_Albania" title="Parliament of Albania">parliament</a>, which is elected every four years by a system of <a href="/wiki/Party-list_proportional_representation" title="Party-list proportional representation">party-list proportional representation</a> by the Albanian people on the basis of free, equal, universal and periodic <a href="/wiki/Suffrage" title="Suffrage">suffrage</a> by <a href="/wiki/Secret_ballot" title="Secret ballot">secret ballot</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-kushtetuta_171-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-kushtetuta-171">&#91;169&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/Civil_law_(legal_system)" title="Civil law (legal system)">civil law</a>, codified and based on the <a href="/wiki/Napoleonic_Code" title="Napoleonic Code">Napoleonic Code</a>, is divided between courts with regular civil and criminal jurisdiction and administrative courts. The <a href="/wiki/Judicial_power" class="mw-redirect" title="Judicial power">judicial power</a> is vested in the <a href="/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_Albania" title="Supreme Court of Albania">supreme court</a>, <a href="/wiki/Constitutional_Court_of_Albania" title="Constitutional Court of Albania">constitutional court</a>, <a href="/wiki/Appeals_courts_of_Albania" title="Appeals courts of Albania">appeal court</a> and <a href="/wiki/Administrative_Courts_in_Albania" class="mw-redirect" title="Administrative Courts in Albania">administrative court</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-172" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-172">&#91;170&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Law_enforcement" title="Law enforcement">Law enforcement</a> in the country is primarily the responsibility of the <a href="/wiki/Albanian_Police" class="mw-redirect" title="Albanian Police">Albanian Police</a>, the main and largest state law enforcement agency. It carries out nearly all general police duties including criminal investigation, patrol activity, traffic policing and border control.
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/Executive_power" class="mw-redirect" title="Executive power">executive power</a> is exercised by the president and prime minister whereby the power of the president is very limited. The president is the <a href="/wiki/Commander-in-chief" title="Commander-in-chief">commander-in-chief</a> of the <a href="/wiki/Albanian_Armed_Forces" title="Albanian Armed Forces">military</a> and the representative of the unity of the Albanian people.<sup id="cite_ref-president_173-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-president-173">&#91;171&#93;</a></sup> The tenure of the president depends on the <a href="/wiki/Confidence_and_supply" title="Confidence and supply">confidence</a> of the parliament and is elected for a five-year <a href="/wiki/Term_of_office" title="Term of office">term</a> by the parliament by a majority of three-fifths of all its members. The prime minister, appointed by the president and approved by the parliament, is authorised to constitute the <a href="/wiki/Cabinet_of_Albania" class="mw-redirect" title="Cabinet of Albania">cabinet</a>. The cabinet is composed primarily of the prime minister inclusively its deputies and ministers.<sup id="cite_ref-prime_minister_174-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-prime_minister-174">&#91;172&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Foreign_relations">Foreign relations</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Foreign_relations_of_Albania" title="Foreign relations of Albania">Foreign relations of Albania</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Artigianato_Arberesh.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/36/Artigianato_Arberesh.jpg/220px-Artigianato_Arberesh.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="172" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/36/Artigianato_Arberesh.jpg/330px-Artigianato_Arberesh.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/36/Artigianato_Arberesh.jpg/440px-Artigianato_Arberesh.jpg 2x" data-file-width="474" data-file-height="371" /></a><figcaption>Assisted by the governments of <a href="/wiki/Kosovo" title="Kosovo">Kosovo</a> and Albania, an official application for the inclusion of the <a href="/wiki/Arb%C3%ABresh%C3%AB_people" title="Arbëreshë people">Arbëreshë people</a> in the list of <a href="/wiki/UNESCO" title="UNESCO">UNESCO</a>'s <a href="/wiki/UNESCO_Intangible_Cultural_Heritage_Lists" title="UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage Lists">Intangible Cultural Heritage</a> is being prepared.<sup id="cite_ref-175" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-175">&#91;173&#93;</a></sup></figcaption></figure>
<p>Emerging from decades of isolation during the communism, Albania has adopted a <a href="/wiki/Foreign_relations_of_Albania" title="Foreign relations of Albania">foreign policy</a> orientation centered on active cooperation and engagement in international affairs. At the core of Albania's foreign policies lie a set of objectives, which encompass the commitment to protect its sovereignty and territorial integrity, the cultivation of diplomatic ties with other countries, advocacy for <a href="/wiki/International_recognition_of_Kosovo" title="International recognition of Kosovo">international recognition of Kosovo</a>, addressing concerns related to the <a href="/wiki/Expulsion_of_Cham_Albanians" title="Expulsion of Cham Albanians">expulsion of Cham Albanians</a>, the pursuit of <a href="/wiki/European_Union" title="European Union">European Union</a> (EU) <a href="/wiki/Accession_of_Albania_to_the_European_Union" title="Accession of Albania to the European Union">membership</a> and safeguarding of the rights of the Albanians in <a href="/wiki/Albanians_in_Kosovo" class="mw-redirect" title="Albanians in Kosovo">Kosovo</a>, <a href="/wiki/Albanians_in_greece" class="mw-redirect" title="Albanians in greece">Greece</a>, <a href="/wiki/Arb%C3%ABresh%C3%AB_people" title="Arbëreshë people">Italy</a>, <a href="/wiki/Albanians_in_Montenegro" title="Albanians in Montenegro">Montenegro</a>, <a href="/wiki/Albanians_in_Macedonia" class="mw-redirect" title="Albanians in Macedonia">North Macedonia</a>, <a href="/wiki/Albanians_in_south_Serbia" class="mw-redirect" title="Albanians in south Serbia">Serbia</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Albanian_diaspora" title="Albanian diaspora">diaspora</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-176" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-176">&#91;174&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The external affairs of Albania underscore the country's dedication to regional stability and integration into major international institutions.<sup id="cite_ref-177" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-177">&#91;175&#93;</a></sup> Albania became a member of the <a href="/wiki/United_Nations" title="United Nations">United Nations</a> (UN) in 1955, shortly after emerging from a period of isolation during the communist era.<sup id="cite_ref-178" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-178">&#91;176&#93;</a></sup> The country reached a major achievement in its foreign policy by securing membership in the <a href="/wiki/NATO" title="NATO">North Atlantic Treaty Organization</a> (NATO) in 2009.<sup id="cite_ref-179" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-179">&#91;177&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-180" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-180">&#91;178&#93;</a></sup> Since obtaining candidate status in 2014, the country has also embarked on a comprehensive reform agenda to align itself with <a href="/wiki/European_Union" title="European Union">European Union</a> (EU) accession standards, with the objective of becoming an EU member state.<sup id="cite_ref-EU_CS_117-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-EU_CS-117">&#91;115&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Albania and Kosovo maintain a fraternal relationship strengthened by their substantial cultural, ethnical and historical ties.<sup id="cite_ref-AlbKosRelation_181-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-AlbKosRelation-181">&#91;179&#93;</a></sup> Both countries foster enduring diplomatic ties, with Albania actively supporting Kosovo's development and international integration efforts.<sup id="cite_ref-AlbKosRelation_181-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-AlbKosRelation-181">&#91;179&#93;</a></sup> Its fundamental contribution to <a href="/wiki/2008_Kosovo_declaration_of_independence" title="2008 Kosovo declaration of independence">Kosovo's path to independence</a> is underscored by its early <a href="/wiki/International_recognition_of_Kosovo" title="International recognition of Kosovo">recognition of Kosovo's sovereignty</a> in 2008.<sup id="cite_ref-182" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-182">&#91;180&#93;</a></sup> Furthermore, both governments hold annual joint meetings, displayed by the inaugural meeting in 2014, which serves as an official platform to enhance bilateral cooperation and reinforce their joint commitment to policies that promote the stability and prosperity of the broader Albanian region.<sup id="cite_ref-AlbKosRelation_181-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-AlbKosRelation-181">&#91;179&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Military">Military</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Armed_Forces_of_Albania" class="mw-redirect" title="Armed Forces of Albania">Armed Forces of Albania</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Albanian_special_operations_forces,_provide_security_as_Afghan_Border_Police_(ABP)_break_ground_on_a_new_checkpoint_in_the_district_of_Spin_Boldak,_Kandahar_province,_Afghanistan,_March_25,_2013_130325-A-MX357-127.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1f/Albanian_special_operations_forces%2C_provide_security_as_Afghan_Border_Police_%28ABP%29_break_ground_on_a_new_checkpoint_in_the_district_of_Spin_Boldak%2C_Kandahar_province%2C_Afghanistan%2C_March_25%2C_2013_130325-A-MX357-127.jpg/220px-thumbnail.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="164" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1f/Albanian_special_operations_forces%2C_provide_security_as_Afghan_Border_Police_%28ABP%29_break_ground_on_a_new_checkpoint_in_the_district_of_Spin_Boldak%2C_Kandahar_province%2C_Afghanistan%2C_March_25%2C_2013_130325-A-MX357-127.jpg/330px-thumbnail.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1f/Albanian_special_operations_forces%2C_provide_security_as_Afghan_Border_Police_%28ABP%29_break_ground_on_a_new_checkpoint_in_the_district_of_Spin_Boldak%2C_Kandahar_province%2C_Afghanistan%2C_March_25%2C_2013_130325-A-MX357-127.jpg/440px-thumbnail.jpg 2x" data-file-width="3332" data-file-height="2480" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Albanian_Land_Force" title="Albanian Land Force">Albanian soldiers</a> in the <a href="/wiki/Kandahar_Province" title="Kandahar Province">Province of Kandahar</a>, Afghanistan</figcaption></figure>
<p>The <a href="/wiki/Albanian_Armed_Forces" title="Albanian Armed Forces">Albanian Armed Forces</a> consist of <a href="/wiki/Albanian_Land_Force" title="Albanian Land Force">Land</a>, <a href="/wiki/Albanian_Air_Force" title="Albanian Air Force">Air</a> and <a href="/wiki/Albanian_Naval_Force" title="Albanian Naval Force">Naval Forces</a> and constitute the military and paramilitary forces of the country. They are led by a <a href="/wiki/Commander-in-chief" title="Commander-in-chief">commander-in-chief</a> under the supervision of the <a href="/wiki/Ministry_of_Defence_(Albania)" title="Ministry of Defence (Albania)">Ministry of Defence</a> and by the <a href="/wiki/President_of_Albania" title="President of Albania">President</a> as the supreme commander during wartime. However, in times of peace its powers are executed through the <a href="/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Albania" title="Prime Minister of Albania">Prime Minister</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Ministry_of_Defence_(Albania)" title="Ministry of Defence (Albania)">Defence Minister</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-constitution_183-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-constitution-183">&#91;181&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The chief purpose of the armed forces of Albania is the defence of the independence, the <a href="/wiki/Sovereignty" title="Sovereignty">sovereignty</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Territorial_integrity" title="Territorial integrity">territorial integrity</a> of the country, as well as the participation in humanitarian, combat, non-combat and peace support operations.<sup id="cite_ref-constitution_183-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-constitution-183">&#91;181&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Military_service" title="Military service">Military service</a> is voluntary since 2010 with the age of 19 being the legal minimum age for the duty.<sup id="cite_ref-184" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-184">&#91;182&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-185" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-185">&#91;183&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Albania has committed to increase the participations in multinational operations.<sup id="cite_ref-186" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-186">&#91;184&#93;</a></sup> Since the fall of communism, the country has participated in six international missions but only one United Nations mission in <a href="/wiki/UNOMIG" class="mw-redirect" title="UNOMIG">Georgia</a>, where it sent three military observers. Since February 2008, Albania has participated officially in NATO's <a href="/wiki/Operation_Active_Endeavor" class="mw-redirect" title="Operation Active Endeavor">Operation Active Endeavor</a> in the <a href="/wiki/Mediterranean_Sea" title="Mediterranean Sea">Mediterranean Sea</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-187" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-187">&#91;185&#93;</a></sup> It was invited to join NATO on 3 April 2008, and it became a full member on 2 April 2009.<sup id="cite_ref-188" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-188">&#91;186&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Albania reduced the number of active troops from 65,000 in 1988 to 14,500 in 2009.<sup id="cite_ref-189" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-189">&#91;187&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-190" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-190">&#91;188&#93;</a></sup> The military now consists mainly of a small fleet of aircraft and sea vessels. Increasing the military budget was one of the most important conditions for <a href="/wiki/NATO" title="NATO">NATO</a> integration. As of 1996 military spending was an estimated 1.5% of the country's GDP, only to peak in 2009 at 2% and fall again to 1.5%.<sup id="cite_ref-191" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-191">&#91;189&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Administrative_divisions">Administrative divisions</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Administrative_divisions_of_Albania" title="Administrative divisions of Albania">Administrative divisions of Albania</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/Counties_of_Albania" title="Counties of Albania">Counties of Albania</a>, <a href="/wiki/Regions_of_Albania" title="Regions of Albania">Regions of Albania</a>, <a href="/wiki/Municipalities_of_Albania" title="Municipalities of Albania">Municipalities of Albania</a>, <a href="/wiki/Communes_of_Albania" title="Communes of Albania">Communes of Albania</a>, <a href="/wiki/List_of_cities_and_towns_in_Albania" title="List of cities and towns in Albania">List of cities and towns in Albania</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Villages_of_Albania" title="Villages of Albania">Villages of Albania</a></div>
<p>Albania is defined within a territorial area of 28,748&#160;km<sup>2</sup> (11,100&#160;sq&#160;mi) in the <a href="/wiki/Balkan_Peninsula" class="mw-redirect" title="Balkan Peninsula">Balkan Peninsula</a>. It is informally divided into three regions, the <a href="/wiki/Northern_Albania" title="Northern Albania">Northern</a>, <a href="/wiki/Central_Albania" title="Central Albania">Central</a> and <a href="/wiki/Southern_Albania" title="Southern Albania">Southern Regions</a>. Since <a href="/wiki/Albanian_Declaration_of_Independence" title="Albanian Declaration of Independence">its Declaration of Independence</a> in 1912, Albania has reformed <a href="/wiki/Administrative_divisions_of_Albania#History" title="Administrative divisions of Albania">its internal organization</a> 21 times. Presently, the primary <a href="/wiki/Administrative_divisions_of_Albania" title="Administrative divisions of Albania">administrative units</a> are the twelve constituent <a href="/wiki/Counties_of_Albania" title="Counties of Albania">counties</a> (<span title="Albanian-language text"><i lang="sq"><span lang="sq"><a href="https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/qarqe#Albanian" class="extiw" title="wikt:qarqe">qarqe</a></span>/<span lang="sq"><a href="https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/qarqet#Albanian" class="extiw" title="wikt:qarqet">qarqet</a></span></i></span>), which hold equal status under the law.<sup id="cite_ref-192" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-192">&#91;190&#93;</a></sup> Counties had previously been used in the 1950s and were recreated on 31 July 2000 to unify the 36 <a href="/wiki/Districts_of_Albania" title="Districts of Albania">districts</a> (<span title="Albanian-language text"><i lang="sq"><span lang="sq"><a href="https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/rrath%C3%AB#Albanian" class="extiw" title="wikt:rrathë">rrathë</a></span>/<span lang="sq"><a href="https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/rrath%C3%ABt#Albanian" class="extiw" title="wikt:rrathët">rrathët</a></span></i></span>) of that time.<sup id="cite_ref-193" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-193">&#91;191&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-terref_194-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-terref-194">&#91;192&#93;</a></sup> The largest county in Albania by population is <a href="/wiki/Tirana_County" title="Tirana County">Tirana County</a> with over 800,000 people. The smallest county, by population, is <a href="/wiki/Gjirokast%C3%ABr_County" title="Gjirokastër County">Gjirokastër County</a> with over 70,000 people. The largest in the county, by area, is <a href="/wiki/Kor%C3%A7%C3%AB_County" title="Korçë County">Korçë County</a> encompassing 3,711 square kilometres (1,433&#160;sq&#160;mi) of the southeast of Albania. The smallest county, by area, is <a href="/wiki/Durr%C3%ABs_County" title="Durrës County">Durrës County</a> with an area of 766 square kilometres (296&#160;sq&#160;mi) in the west of Albania.
</p><p>The counties are made up of 61 second-level divisions known as <a href="/wiki/Municipalities_of_Albania" title="Municipalities of Albania">municipalities</a> (<span title="Albanian-language text"><i lang="sq"><span lang="sq"><a href="https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/bashki#Albanian" class="extiw" title="wikt:bashki">bashki</a></span>/<span lang="sq"><a href="https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/bashkia#Albanian" class="extiw" title="wikt:bashkia">bashkia</a></span></i></span>).<sup id="cite_ref-195" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-195">&#91;193&#93;</a></sup> The municipalities are the first level of local governance, responsible for local needs and <a href="/wiki/Law_enforcement_in_Albania" title="Law enforcement in Albania">law enforcement</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-196" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-196">&#91;194&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-197" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-197">&#91;195&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-198" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-198">&#91;196&#93;</a></sup> They unified and simplified the previous system of <a href="/wiki/Urban_municipalities_of_Albania" class="mw-redirect" title="Urban municipalities of Albania">urban</a> and <a href="/wiki/Rural_municipalities_of_Albania" class="mw-redirect" title="Rural municipalities of Albania">rural municipalities</a> or <a href="/wiki/Communes_of_Albania" title="Communes of Albania">communes</a> (<span title="Albanian-language text"><i lang="sq"><span lang="sq"><a href="https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/komuna#Albanian" class="extiw" title="wikt:komuna">komuna</a></span>/<span lang="sq"><a href="https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/komunat#Albanian" class="extiw" title="wikt:komunat">komunat</a></span></i></span>) in 2015.<sup id="cite_ref-199" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-199">&#91;197&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-200" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-200">&#91;198&#93;</a></sup> For smaller issues of <a href="/wiki/Local_government" title="Local government">local government</a>, the municipalities are organized into 373 <a href="/wiki/Administrative_units_of_Albania" class="mw-redirect" title="Administrative units of Albania">administrative units</a> (<span title="Albanian-language text"><i lang="sq">njësia</i></span>/<span title="Albanian-language text"><i lang="sq">njësitë administrative</i></span>). There are also 2980 villages (<span title="Albanian-language text"><i lang="sq"><span lang="sq"><a href="https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/fshatra#Albanian" class="extiw" title="wikt:fshatra">fshatra</a></span>/<span lang="sq"><a href="https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/fshatrat#Albanian" class="extiw" title="wikt:fshatrat">fshatrat</a></span></i></span>), neighborhoods or wards (<span title="Albanian-language text"><i lang="sq"><span lang="sq"><a href="https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/lagje#Albanian" class="extiw" title="wikt:lagje">lagje</a></span>/<span lang="sq"><a href="https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/lagjet#Albanian" class="extiw" title="wikt:lagjet">lagjet</a></span></i></span>), and localities (<span title="Albanian-language text"><i lang="sq"><span lang="sq"><a href="https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/lokalitete#Albanian" class="extiw" title="wikt:lokalitete">lokalitete</a></span>/<span lang="sq"><a href="https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/lokalitetet#Albanian" class="extiw" title="wikt:lokalitetet">lokalitetet</a></span></i></span>) previously used as administrative units.
</p>
