<div class="thumbcaption">
<p><a href="/wiki/Religion_in_Albania" title="Religion in Albania">Religion in Albania</a> as of the 2011 census conducted by the <a href="/wiki/Institute_of_Statistics_(Albania)" title="Institute of Statistics (Albania)">Institute of Statistics</a> (INSTAT)<sup id="cite_ref-Religion_2011_Census_314-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Religion_2011_Census-314">&#91;312&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<style data-mw-deduplicate="TemplateStyles:r981673959">.mw-parser-output .legend{page-break-inside:avoid;break-inside:avoid-column}.mw-parser-output .legend-color{display:inline-block;min-width:1.25em;height:1.25em;line-height:1.25;margin:1px 0;text-align:center;border:1px solid black;background-color:transparent;color:black}.mw-parser-output .legend-text{}</style><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:Green; color:white;">&#160;</span>&#160;<a href="/wiki/Islam_in_Albania" title="Islam in Albania">Islam</a> (58.79%)</div><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:Gold; color:black;">&#160;</span>&#160;<a href="/wiki/Christianity_in_Albania" title="Christianity in Albania">Christianity</a> (16.99%)</div><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:Red; color:black;">&#160;</span>&#160;No Denomination (5.49%)</div><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:Black; color:white;">&#160;</span>&#160;<a href="/wiki/Irreligion_in_Albania" title="Irreligion in Albania">Irreligion</a> (2.5%)</div><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:LightBlue; color:black;">&#160;</span>&#160;Unclear (16.24%)</div>
</div>
</div></div>
<p>Albania is a <a href="/wiki/Secular_state" title="Secular state">secular</a> and religiously diverse country with no <a href="/wiki/Official_religion" class="mw-redirect" title="Official religion">official religion</a> and thus, <a href="/wiki/Freedom_of_religion" title="Freedom of religion">freedom of religion</a>, <a href="/wiki/Freedom_of_belief" class="mw-redirect" title="Freedom of belief">belief</a> and <a href="/wiki/Freedom_of_conscience" class="mw-redirect" title="Freedom of conscience">conscience</a> are guaranteed under the country's <a href="/wiki/Constitution_of_Albania" title="Constitution of Albania">constitution</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-315" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-315">&#91;313&#93;</a></sup> As of the <a href="/wiki/2011_Census_of_Albania" class="mw-redirect" title="2011 Census of Albania">2011 census</a>, there were 1,587,608 (56.7%) <a href="/wiki/Sunni_Islam" title="Sunni Islam">Sunni Muslims</a>, 280,921 (10.03%) <a href="/wiki/Roman_Catholicism" class="mw-redirect" title="Roman Catholicism">Roman Catholics</a>, 188,992 (6.75%) <a href="/wiki/Eastern_Orthodoxy" title="Eastern Orthodoxy">Eastern Orthodox</a>, 58,628 (2.09%) <a href="/wiki/Bektashi_Order" title="Bektashi Order">Bektashi Muslims</a>, 3,797 (0.14%) <a href="/wiki/Evangelicalism" title="Evangelicalism">Evangelicals</a>, 1,919 (0.07%) other <a href="/wiki/Christians" title="Christians">Christians</a>, 602 (0.02%) of other religions and 153,630 (5.49%) believers without denomination in Albania.<sup id="cite_ref-Religion_2011_Census_314-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Religion_2011_Census-314">&#91;312&#93;</a></sup> 69,995 people (2.5%) were <a href="/wiki/Atheism" title="Atheism">irreligious</a> while 386,024 (13.79%) did not declare their religion.<sup id="cite_ref-Religion_2011_Census_314-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Religion_2011_Census-314">&#91;312&#93;</a></sup> Albania is nevertheless ranked among the least religious countries in the world.<sup id="cite_ref-316" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-316">&#91;314&#93;</a></sup> Religion constitute an important role in the lives of only 39% of the country's population.<sup id="cite_ref-317" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-317">&#91;315&#93;</a></sup> In another report, 56% considered themselves religious, 30% considered themselves non-religious, while 9% defined themselves as convinced atheists. 80% believed in God.<sup id="cite_ref-318" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-318">&#91;316&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The preliminary results of the 2011 census seemed to give widely different results, with 70% of respondents refusing to declare belief in any of the listed faiths.<sup id="cite_ref-319" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-319">&#91;317&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-320" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-320">&#91;318&#93;</a></sup> The Albanian Orthodox Church officially refused to recognize the results, claiming that 24% of the total population adhered to its faith.<sup id="cite_ref-321" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-321">&#91;319&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-322" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-322">&#91;320&#93;</a></sup> Some Muslim Community officials expressed unhappiness with the data claiming that many Muslims were not counted and that the number of adherents numbered some 70% of the Albanian population.<sup id="cite_ref-323" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-323">&#91;321&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Jazexhi22_324-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Jazexhi22-324">&#91;322&#93;</a></sup> The Albanian Catholic Bishops Conference also cast doubts on the census, complaining that many of its believers were not contacted.<sup id="cite_ref-325" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-325">&#91;323&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Islam_in_Albania" title="Islam in Albania">Muslim Albanians</a> are spread throughout the country. <a href="/wiki/Orthodoxy_in_Albania" class="mw-redirect" title="Orthodoxy in Albania">Orthodox</a> and <a href="/wiki/Bektashi" class="mw-redirect" title="Bektashi">Bektashis</a> are mostly found in the south, whereas <a href="/wiki/Catholicism_in_Albania" class="mw-redirect" title="Catholicism in Albania">Catholics</a> mainly live in the north.<sup id="cite_ref-International_Religious_Freedom_Report_2007_326-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-International_Religious_Freedom_Report_2007-326">&#91;324&#93;</a></sup> In 2008, there were 694 <a href="/wiki/Catholic" class="mw-redirect" title="Catholic">Catholic</a> churches and 425 <a href="/wiki/Eastern_Orthodox_Church" title="Eastern Orthodox Church">orthodox</a> churches, 568 mosques and 70 <a href="/wiki/Bektashi_Order" title="Bektashi Order">bektashi</a> <a href="/wiki/Khanqah" title="Khanqah">tekkes</a> in the country.<sup id="cite_ref-327" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-327">&#91;325&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-328" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-328">&#91;326&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Marche_Charlie_Hebdo_Paris_02.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/58/Marche_Charlie_Hebdo_Paris_02.jpg/220px-Marche_Charlie_Hebdo_Paris_02.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="149" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/58/Marche_Charlie_Hebdo_Paris_02.jpg/330px-Marche_Charlie_Hebdo_Paris_02.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/58/Marche_Charlie_Hebdo_Paris_02.jpg/440px-Marche_Charlie_Hebdo_Paris_02.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2000" data-file-height="1359" /></a><figcaption>Representatives of the Sunni, Orthodox, Bektashi and Catholic Albanian communities in <a href="/wiki/Paris" title="Paris">Paris</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>During <a href="/wiki/Modern_history" class="mw-redirect" title="Modern history">modern times</a>, the Albanian republican, monarchic and later communist regimes followed a systematic policy of separating religion from official functions and cultural life. The country has never had an <a href="/wiki/Official_religion" class="mw-redirect" title="Official religion">official religion</a> either as a republic or as a kingdom. In the 20th century, the clergy of all faiths was weakened under the monarchy and ultimately eradicated during the 1950s and 1960s, under the state policy of obliterating all organised religion from the territories of Albania. The <a href="/wiki/Communism_in_Albania" class="mw-redirect" title="Communism in Albania">communist regime</a> persecuted and suppressed religious observance and institutions and entirely <a href="/wiki/Anti-religious" class="mw-redirect" title="Anti-religious">banned religion</a>. The country was then officially declared to be the world's first <a href="/wiki/Atheist_state" class="mw-redirect" title="Atheist state">atheist state</a>. Religious freedom has returned, however, since the <a href="/wiki/Fall_of_communism_in_Albania" title="Fall of communism in Albania">end of communism</a>.
</p><p>Islam survived communist era persecution and reemerged in the modern era as a practised religion in Albania.<sup id="cite_ref-Merdjanova673940_329-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Merdjanova673940-329">&#91;327&#93;</a></sup> Some smaller Christian sects in Albania include <a href="/wiki/Evangelicalism" title="Evangelicalism">Evangelicals</a> and several <a href="/wiki/Protestant" class="mw-redirect" title="Protestant">Protestant</a> communities including <a href="/wiki/Seventh-day_Adventist_Church" title="Seventh-day Adventist Church">Seventh-day Adventist Church</a>, <a href="/wiki/The_Church_of_Jesus_Christ_of_Latter-day_Saints" title="The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints">Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints</a> and <a href="/wiki/Jehovah%27s_Witnesses" title="Jehovah&#39;s Witnesses">Jehovah's Witnesses</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-330" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-330">&#91;328&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-331" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-331">&#91;329&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-332" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-332">&#91;330&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-333" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-333">&#91;331&#93;</a></sup> The first recorded Protestant of Albania was Said Toptani, who travelled around Europe and returned to <a href="/wiki/Tirana" title="Tirana">Tirana</a> in 1853, where he preached <a href="/wiki/Protestantism" title="Protestantism">Protestantism</a>. The first <a href="/wiki/Evangelical_Protestants" class="mw-redirect" title="Evangelical Protestants">evangelical Protestants</a> appeared in the 19th century and the Evangelical Alliance was founded in 1892. Nowadays, it has 160 member congregations from different Protestant denominations. Following mass emigration to Israel after the fall of communism, there are only 200 Albanian <a href="/wiki/Judaism_in_Albania" class="mw-redirect" title="Judaism in Albania">Jews</a> left in the country.<sup id="cite_ref-334" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-334">&#91;332&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-335" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-335">&#91;333&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Culture">Culture</span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Culture_of_Albania" title="Culture of Albania">Culture of Albania</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/Albanian_folk_beliefs" title="Albanian folk beliefs">Albanian folk beliefs</a></div>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Symbols">Symbols</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/National_symbols_of_Albania" title="National symbols of Albania">National symbols of Albania</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1097763485"><table class="box-More_citations_needed plainlinks metadata ambox ambox-content ambox-Refimprove" role="presentation"><tbody><tr><td class="mbox-image"><div class="mbox-image-div"><span typeof="mw:File"><a href="/wiki/File:Question_book-new.svg" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/9/99/Question_book-new.svg/50px-Question_book-new.svg.png" decoding="async" width="50" height="39" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/9/99/Question_book-new.svg/75px-Question_book-new.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/9/99/Question_book-new.svg/100px-Question_book-new.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="512" data-file-height="399" /></a></span></div></td><td class="mbox-text"><div class="mbox-text-span">This section <b>needs additional citations for <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability" title="Wikipedia:Verifiability">verification</a></b>.<span class="hide-when-compact"> Please help <a href="/wiki/Special:EditPage/Albania" title="Special:EditPage/Albania">improve this article</a> by <a href="/wiki/Help:Referencing_for_beginners" title="Help:Referencing for beginners">adding citations to reliable sources</a>&#32;in this section. Unsourced material may be challenged and removed.<br /><small><span class="plainlinks"><i>Find sources:</i>&#160;<a rel="nofollow" class="external text" href="https://www.google.com/search?as_eq=wikipedia&amp;q=%22Albania%22">"Albania"</a>&#160;–&#160;<a rel="nofollow" class="external text" href="https://www.google.com/search?tbm=nws&amp;q=%22Albania%22+-wikipedia&amp;tbs=ar:1">news</a>&#160;<b>·</b> <a rel="nofollow" class="external text" href="https://www.google.com/search?&amp;q=%22Albania%22&amp;tbs=bkt:s&amp;tbm=bks">newspapers</a>&#160;<b>·</b> <a rel="nofollow" class="external text" href="https://www.google.com/search?tbs=bks:1&amp;q=%22Albania%22+-wikipedia">books</a>&#160;<b>·</b> <a rel="nofollow" class="external text" href="https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=%22Albania%22">scholar</a>&#160;<b>·</b> <a rel="nofollow" class="external text" href="https://www.jstor.org/action/doBasicSearch?Query=%22Albania%22&amp;acc=on&amp;wc=on">JSTOR</a></span></small></span>  <span class="date-container"><i>(<span class="date">February 2020</span>)</i></span><span class="hide-when-compact"><i> (<small><a href="/wiki/Help:Maintenance_template_removal" title="Help:Maintenance template removal">Learn how and when to remove this template message</a></small>)</i></span></div></td></tr></tbody></table>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Doppeladler_Albanien.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0a/Doppeladler_Albanien.jpg/220px-Doppeladler_Albanien.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="159" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0a/Doppeladler_Albanien.jpg/330px-Doppeladler_Albanien.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0a/Doppeladler_Albanien.jpg/440px-Doppeladler_Albanien.jpg 2x" data-file-width="994" data-file-height="720" /></a><figcaption>The <a href="/wiki/Double-headed_eagle" title="Double-headed eagle">double-headed eagle</a> on the walls of the <a href="/wiki/St._Anthony_Church,_Durr%C3%ABs" title="St. Anthony Church, Durrës">St. Anthony Church</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>Albania shares many symbols associated with its history, culture and belief. These include the colours red and black, animals such as the <a href="/wiki/Golden_eagle" title="Golden eagle">golden eagle</a> living across the country, costumes such as the <a href="/wiki/Fustanella" title="Fustanella">fustanella</a>, <a href="/wiki/Qeleshe" title="Qeleshe">plis</a> and <a href="/wiki/Opinga" title="Opinga">opinga</a> which are worn to special events and celebrations, plants such as the <a href="/wiki/Olive" title="Olive">olive</a> and <a href="/wiki/Papaver_rhoeas" title="Papaver rhoeas">red poppy</a> growing as well across the country.
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/Flag_of_Albania" title="Flag of Albania">flag of Albania</a> is a red flag with a black <a href="/wiki/Double-headed_eagle" title="Double-headed eagle">double-headed eagle</a> positioned in the centre.<sup id="cite_ref-Flamuri_336-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Flamuri-336">&#91;334&#93;</a></sup> The red colour used in the flag symbolises the bravery, strength and valour of the <a href="/wiki/Albanian_people" class="mw-redirect" title="Albanian people">Albanian people</a>, while the black colour appears as a symbol of freedom and heroism.<sup id="cite_ref-Flamuri_336-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Flamuri-336">&#91;334&#93;</a></sup> The eagle has been used by Albanians since the <a href="/wiki/Middle_Ages" title="Middle Ages">Middle Ages</a> including the establishment of the <a href="/wiki/Principality_of_Arb%C3%ABr" class="mw-redirect" title="Principality of Arbër">Principality of Arbër</a> and by numerous noble ruling families such as the <a href="/wiki/Kastrioti_family" class="mw-redirect" title="Kastrioti family">Kastrioti</a>, <a href="/wiki/Muzaka_family" title="Muzaka family">Muzaka</a>, <a href="/wiki/Thopia_family" title="Thopia family">Thopia</a> and <a href="/wiki/Dukagjini_family" title="Dukagjini family">Dukagjini</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-337" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-337">&#91;335&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Gjergj_Kastrioti_Sk%C3%ABnderbeu" class="mw-redirect" title="Gjergj Kastrioti Skënderbeu">Gjergj Kastrioti Skënderbeu</a>, who fought and began a rebellion against the <a href="/wiki/Ottoman_Empire" title="Ottoman Empire">Ottoman Empire</a> which halted Ottoman advance into Europe for nearly 25 years, placed the double-headed eagle on his flag and seal.<sup id="cite_ref-338" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-338">&#91;336&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-339" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-339">&#91;337&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The country's national motto, <i><a href="/wiki/Ti_Shqip%C3%ABri,_m%C3%AB_jep_nder,_m%C3%AB_jep_emrin_Shqip%C3%ABtar" title="Ti Shqipëri, më jep nder, më jep emrin Shqipëtar">Ti Shqipëri, më jep nder, më jep emrin Shqipëtar</a></i> ("You Albania, you give me honour, you give me the name Albanian"), finds its origins in the <a href="/wiki/Albanian_National_Awakening" title="Albanian National Awakening">Albanian National Awakening</a>. The first to express this motto was <a href="/wiki/Naim_Frash%C3%ABri" title="Naim Frashëri">Naim Frashëri</a> in his poem <i>Ti Shqipëri më jep nder</i>.<sup id="cite_ref-340" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-340">&#91;338&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Art_and_architecture">Art and architecture</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/Albanian_art" title="Albanian art">Albanian art</a> and <a href="/wiki/Albanian_architecture" class="mw-redirect" title="Albanian architecture">architecture</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Amphitheatre_of_Butrint_2009.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9b/Amphitheatre_of_Butrint_2009.jpg/220px-Amphitheatre_of_Butrint_2009.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9b/Amphitheatre_of_Butrint_2009.jpg/330px-Amphitheatre_of_Butrint_2009.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9b/Amphitheatre_of_Butrint_2009.jpg/440px-Amphitheatre_of_Butrint_2009.jpg 2x" data-file-width="3872" data-file-height="2592" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Butrint" title="Butrint">Butrint</a> has been included in the <a href="/wiki/UNESCO" title="UNESCO">UNESCO</a> list of <a href="/wiki/World_Heritage_Site" title="World Heritage Site">World Heritage Sites</a> since 1992.</figcaption></figure>
<p>The <a href="/wiki/Albanian_art" title="Albanian art">artistic history</a> of Albania has been particularly influenced by a multitude of ancient and medieval <a href="/wiki/Civilisation" class="mw-redirect" title="Civilisation">people</a>, traditions and religions. It covers a broad spectrum with mediums and disciplines that include painting, <a href="/wiki/Pottery" title="Pottery">pottery</a>, sculpture, <a href="/wiki/Ceramic" title="Ceramic">ceramics</a> and architecture all of them exemplifying a great variety in style and shape, in different regions and period.
</p><p>The rise of the <a href="/wiki/Byzantine_Empire" title="Byzantine Empire">Byzantine</a> and <a href="/wiki/Ottoman_Empire" title="Ottoman Empire">Ottoman Empire</a> in the <a href="/wiki/Middle_Ages" title="Middle Ages">Middle Ages</a> was accompanied by a corresponding growth in <a href="/wiki/Christian_art" title="Christian art">Christian</a> and <a href="/wiki/Islamic_art" title="Islamic art">Islamic art</a> in the lands of Albania which are apparent in examples of architecture and mosaics throughout the country.<sup id="cite_ref-www.albanianart.net_index_al_341-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-www.albanianart.net_index_al-341">&#91;339&#93;</a></sup> Centuries later, the <a href="/wiki/Albanian_Renaissance" class="mw-redirect" title="Albanian Renaissance">Albanian Renaissance</a> proved crucial to the emancipation of the modern Albanian culture and saw unprecedented developments in all fields of literature and art whereas artists sought to return to the ideals of <a href="/wiki/Impressionism" title="Impressionism">Impressionism</a> and <a href="/wiki/Romanticism_(art)" class="mw-redirect" title="Romanticism (art)">Romanticism</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-342" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-342">&#91;340&#93;</a></sup> However, <a href="/wiki/Onufri" title="Onufri">Onufri</a>, <a href="/wiki/Kol%C3%AB_Idromeno" title="Kolë Idromeno">Kolë Idromeno</a>, <a href="/wiki/David_Selenica" title="David Selenica">David Selenica</a>, <a href="/wiki/Kostandin_Shpataraku" title="Kostandin Shpataraku">Kostandin Shpataraku</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Zografi_Brothers" title="Zografi Brothers">Zografi Brothers</a> are the most eminent representatives of Albanian art.
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/Architecture_of_Albania" title="Architecture of Albania">architecture of Albania</a> reflects the legacy of various civilisations tracing back to the <a href="/wiki/Classical_antiquity" title="Classical antiquity">classical antiquity</a>. Major cities in Albania have evolved from within the castle to include dwellings, religious and commercial structures, with constant redesigning of town squares and evolution of building techniques. Nowadays, the cities and towns reflect a whole spectrum of various <a href="/wiki/Architectural_style" title="Architectural style">architectural styles</a>. In the 20th century, many historical as well as <a href="/wiki/Sacred_architecture" class="mw-redirect" title="Sacred architecture">sacred</a> buildings bearing the ancient influence were demolished during the <a href="/wiki/Communism_in_Albania" class="mw-redirect" title="Communism in Albania">communist era</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-343" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-343">&#91;341&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p><a href="/wiki/Ancient_architecture" class="mw-redirect" title="Ancient architecture">Ancient architecture</a> is found throughout Albania and most visible in <a href="/wiki/Byllis" title="Byllis">Byllis</a>, <a href="/wiki/Amantia" title="Amantia">Amantia</a>, <a href="/wiki/Phoenice" title="Phoenice">Phoenice</a>, <a href="/wiki/Apollonia_(Illyria)" title="Apollonia (Illyria)">Apollonia</a>, <a href="/wiki/Butrint" title="Butrint">Butrint</a>, <a href="/wiki/Antigonia_(Chaonia)" title="Antigonia (Chaonia)">Antigonia</a>, <a href="/wiki/Rozafa_Castle" title="Rozafa Castle">Shkodër</a> and <a href="/wiki/Durr%C3%ABs_Amphitheatre" class="mw-redirect" title="Durrës Amphitheatre">Durrës</a>. Considering the long period of rule of the <a href="/wiki/Byzantine_Empire" title="Byzantine Empire">Byzantine Empire</a>, they introduced castles, citadels, churches and monasteries with spectacular wealth of visible <a href="/wiki/Mural" title="Mural">murals</a> and <a href="/wiki/Fresco" title="Fresco">frescos</a>. Perhaps the best known examples can be found in the southern Albanian cities and surroundings of <a href="/wiki/Kor%C3%A7%C3%AB" title="Korçë">Korçë</a>, <a href="/wiki/Berat" title="Berat">Berat</a>, <a href="/wiki/Voskopoj%C3%AB" class="mw-redirect" title="Voskopojë">Voskopojë</a> and <a href="/wiki/Gjirokast%C3%ABr" title="Gjirokastër">Gjirokastër</a>. Involving the introduction of <a href="/wiki/Ottoman_architecture" title="Ottoman architecture">Ottoman architecture</a> there was a development of mosques and other Islamic buildings, particularly seen in Berat and Gjirokastër.
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Bliss_by_Helidon_Xhixza.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/a/a7/Bliss_by_Helidon_Xhixza.jpg/220px-Bliss_by_Helidon_Xhixza.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/a/a7/Bliss_by_Helidon_Xhixza.jpg/330px-Bliss_by_Helidon_Xhixza.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/a/a7/Bliss_by_Helidon_Xhixza.jpg/440px-Bliss_by_Helidon_Xhixza.jpg 2x" data-file-width="640" data-file-height="427" /></a><figcaption><i>Bliss</i>, stainless steel sculpture by contemporary artist <a href="/wiki/Helidon_Xhixha" title="Helidon Xhixha">Helidon Xhixha</a>.</figcaption></figure>
<p>A productive period of <a href="/wiki/Historicism_(art)" title="Historicism (art)">Historicism</a>, <a href="/wiki/Art_Nouveau" title="Art Nouveau">Art Nouveau</a> and <a href="/wiki/Neoclassicism" title="Neoclassicism">Neoclassicism</a> merged into the 19th century, best exemplified in <a href="/wiki/Kor%C3%A7%C3%AB" title="Korçë">Korçë</a>. The 20th century brought new architectural styles such as the modern <a href="/wiki/Italianate_architecture" title="Italianate architecture">Italian style</a>, which is present in <a href="/wiki/Tirana" title="Tirana">Tirana</a> such as the <a href="/wiki/Skanderbeg_Square" title="Skanderbeg Square">Skanderbeg Square</a> and Ministries. It is also present in Shkodër, <a href="/wiki/Vlor%C3%AB" title="Vlorë">Vlorë</a>, <a href="/wiki/Sarand%C3%AB" title="Sarandë">Sarandë</a> and <a href="/wiki/Durr%C3%ABs" title="Durrës">Durrës</a>. Moreover, other towns received their present-day Albania-unique appearance through various cultural or economic influences.
</p><p><a href="/wiki/Socialist_classicism" class="mw-redirect" title="Socialist classicism">Socialist classicism</a> arrived during the <a href="/wiki/Peoples_Republic_of_Albania" class="mw-redirect" title="Peoples Republic of Albania">communist era</a> in Albania after the <a href="/wiki/Second_World_War" class="mw-redirect" title="Second World War">Second World War</a>. At this period many socialist-styled complexes, wide roads and factories were constructed, while town squares were redesigned and numerous of historic and important buildings demolished. Notable examples of that style include the <a href="/wiki/Mother_Teresa_Square_(Tirana)" title="Mother Teresa Square (Tirana)">Mother Teresa Square</a>, <a href="/wiki/Pyramid_of_Tirana" title="Pyramid of Tirana">Pyramid of Tirana</a>, <a href="/wiki/Palace_of_Congresses" title="Palace of Congresses">Palace of Congresses</a> and so on.
</p><p>Three Albanian archaeological sites are included in the list of <a href="/wiki/UNESCO_World_Heritage_Site" class="mw-redirect" title="UNESCO World Heritage Site">UNESCO World Heritage Sites</a>. These include the ancient remains of Butrint, the medieval <a href="/wiki/Historic_Centres_of_Berat_and_Gjirokast%C3%ABr" title="Historic Centres of Berat and Gjirokastër">Historic Centres of Berat and Gjirokastër</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Ohrid_Lake" class="mw-redirect" title="Ohrid Lake">Natural and Cultural Heritage of the Ohrid region</a> site shared with <a href="/wiki/North_Macedonia" title="North Macedonia">North Macedonia</a> since 2019.<sup id="cite_ref-344" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-344">&#91;342&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-345" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-345">&#91;343&#93;</a></sup> Furthermore, the royal <a href="/wiki/Royal_Tombs_of_Selca_e_Poshtme" title="Royal Tombs of Selca e Poshtme">Illyrian tombs</a>, the remains of <a href="/wiki/Apollonia_(Illyria)" title="Apollonia (Illyria)">Apollonia</a>, the ancient <a href="/wiki/Durr%C3%ABs_Amphitheatre" class="mw-redirect" title="Durrës Amphitheatre">Amphitheatre</a> of Durrës and the <a href="/wiki/Fortress_of_Bashtov%C3%AB" title="Fortress of Bashtovë">Fortress of Bashtovë</a> has been included on the tentative list of Albania.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Cuisine">Cuisine</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Albanian_cuisine" title="Albanian cuisine">Albanian cuisine</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Buk%C3%AB_kollomoqe,_buk%C3%AB_misri.JPG" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1f/Buk%C3%AB_kollomoqe%2C_buk%C3%AB_misri.JPG/220px-Buk%C3%AB_kollomoqe%2C_buk%C3%AB_misri.JPG" decoding="async" width="220" height="165" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1f/Buk%C3%AB_kollomoqe%2C_buk%C3%AB_misri.JPG/330px-Buk%C3%AB_kollomoqe%2C_buk%C3%AB_misri.JPG 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1f/Buk%C3%AB_kollomoqe%2C_buk%C3%AB_misri.JPG/440px-Buk%C3%AB_kollomoqe%2C_buk%C3%AB_misri.JPG 2x" data-file-width="4000" data-file-height="3000" /></a><figcaption>Bukë misri (<a href="/wiki/Cornbread" title="Cornbread">cornbread</a>) is a staple on the Albanian table.</figcaption></figure>
<p>Throughout the centuries, <a href="/wiki/Albanian_cuisine" title="Albanian cuisine">Albanian cuisine</a> has been widely influenced by <a href="/wiki/Albanian_culture" class="mw-redirect" title="Albanian culture">Albanian culture</a>, <a href="/wiki/Geography_of_Albania" title="Geography of Albania">geography</a> and <a href="/wiki/History_of_Albania" title="History of Albania">history</a>, and as such, different parts of the country enjoy specific <a href="/wiki/Regional_cuisine" title="Regional cuisine">regional cuisines</a>. Cooking traditions especially vary between the north and the south, owing to differing <a href="/wiki/Topography" title="Topography">topography</a> and <a href="/wiki/Climate" title="Climate">climate</a> that essentially contribute to the excellent growth conditions for a wide array of herbs, fruits, and vegetables.<sup id="cite_ref-346" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-346">&#91;344&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Albanians produce and use many varieties of fruits such as <a href="/wiki/Lemon_(fruit)" class="mw-redirect" title="Lemon (fruit)">lemons</a>, oranges, <a href="/wiki/Figs_(fruit)" class="mw-redirect" title="Figs (fruit)">figs</a>, and most notably, <a href="/wiki/Olive_(fruit)" class="mw-redirect" title="Olive (fruit)">olives</a>, which are perhaps the most important element of Albanian cooking. Spices and other herbs such as <a href="/wiki/Basil_(herb)" class="mw-redirect" title="Basil (herb)">basil</a>, <a href="/wiki/Lavender" class="mw-redirect" title="Lavender">lavender</a>, <a href="/wiki/Spearmint" title="Spearmint">mint</a>, <a href="/wiki/Oregano" title="Oregano">oregano</a>, <a href="/wiki/Rosemary" title="Rosemary">rosemary</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Thyme" title="Thyme">thyme</a> are widely used, as are vegetables such as garlic, onions, <a href="/wiki/Bell_pepper" title="Bell pepper">peppers</a>, potatoes, tomatoes, as well as <a href="/wiki/Legume" title="Legume">legumes</a> of all types.
</p><p>With a coastline along the <a href="/wiki/Albanian_Adriatic_Sea_Coast" title="Albanian Adriatic Sea Coast">Adriatic</a> and <a href="/wiki/Albanian_Ionian_Sea_Coast" title="Albanian Ionian Sea Coast">Ionian</a> in the <a href="/wiki/Mediterranean_Sea" title="Mediterranean Sea">Mediterranean Sea</a>, fish, <a href="/wiki/Crustacean" title="Crustacean">crustaceans</a>, and seafood are a popular and an integral part of the Albanian diet. Otherwise, <a href="/wiki/Lamb_(food)" class="mw-redirect" title="Lamb (food)">lamb</a> is the traditional meat for different holidays and <a href="/wiki/Religious_festival" title="Religious festival">religious festivals</a> for both <a href="/wiki/Christianity_in_Albania" title="Christianity in Albania">Christians</a> and <a href="/wiki/Islam_in_Albania" title="Islam in Albania">Muslims</a>, although poultry, beef, and pork are also in plentiful supply.
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Albanian_cuisine_-_Pite_dhe_Speca.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2f/Albanian_cuisine_-_Pite_dhe_Speca.jpg/220px-Albanian_cuisine_-_Pite_dhe_Speca.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="211" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2f/Albanian_cuisine_-_Pite_dhe_Speca.jpg/330px-Albanian_cuisine_-_Pite_dhe_Speca.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2f/Albanian_cuisine_-_Pite_dhe_Speca.jpg/440px-Albanian_cuisine_-_Pite_dhe_Speca.jpg 2x" data-file-width="3456" data-file-height="3314" /></a><figcaption>Speca të ferguara (roasted <a href="/wiki/Capsicum" title="Capsicum">peppers</a>) served with <a href="/wiki/Pite_(food)" class="mw-redirect" title="Pite (food)">pite</a>, a traditional and prominent layered Albanian pie</figcaption></figure>
<p><a href="/wiki/Tav%C3%AB_kosi" title="Tavë kosi">Tavë kosi</a> ("<a href="/wiki/Soured_milk" title="Soured milk">soured milk</a> <a href="/wiki/Casserole" title="Casserole">casserole</a>") is the <a href="/wiki/National_dish" title="National dish">national dish</a> of Albania, consisting of lamb and rice baked under a thick, tart veil of <a href="/wiki/Yoghurt" class="mw-redirect" title="Yoghurt">yoghurt</a>. Fërgesë is another national dish, made up of peppers, tomatoes, and <a href="/wiki/Cottage_cheese" title="Cottage cheese">cottage cheese</a>. Pite is also popular, a baked pastry with a filling of a mixture of <a href="/wiki/Spinach" title="Spinach">spinach</a> and gjizë (curd) or mish (<a href="/wiki/Ground_meat" title="Ground meat">ground meat</a>).
</p><p>Petulla, a traditional fried dough, is also a popular speciality, and is served with <a href="/wiki/Powdered_sugar" title="Powdered sugar">powdered sugar</a> or <a href="/wiki/Feta_cheese" class="mw-redirect" title="Feta cheese">feta cheese</a> and different sorts of <a href="/wiki/Fruit_preserves" title="Fruit preserves">fruit jams</a>. <a href="/wiki/Flia" title="Flia">Flia</a> consists of multiple <a href="/wiki/Cr%C3%AApe" title="Crêpe">crêpe</a>-like layers brushed with cream and served with sour cream. <a href="/wiki/Krofne" title="Krofne">Krofne</a>, similar to <a href="/wiki/Berliner_(doughnut)" title="Berliner (doughnut)">Berliner doughnuts</a>, are filled with jam, or chocolate and often eaten during winter.
</p><p>Coffee is an integral part of the Albanian lifestyle. The country has more coffee houses per capita than any other country in the world.<sup id="cite_ref-347" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-347">&#91;345&#93;</a></sup> Tea is also enjoyed both at home or outside at cafés, bars, or restaurants. Çaj Mali (<a href="/wiki/Sideritis" title="Sideritis">Sideritis</a> tea) is enormously beloved, and a part of the daily routine for most Albanians. It is cultivated across Southern Albania and noted for its medicinal properties. <a href="/wiki/Black_tea" title="Black tea">Black tea</a> is also popular.
</p><p><a href="/wiki/Albanian_wine" title="Albanian wine">Albanian wine</a> is also common throughout the country, and has been cultivated for thousands of years. Albania has a long and ancient history of wine production, and belongs to the <a href="/wiki/Old_World_wine" title="Old World wine">Old World of wine producing countries</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-348" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-348">&#91;346&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-349" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-349">&#91;347&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<div style="clear:both;"></div>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Media">Media</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Media_in_Albania" class="mw-redirect" title="Media in Albania">Media in Albania</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/Cinema_of_Albania" title="Cinema of Albania">Cinema of Albania</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Villa_of_the_former_Radio_Tirana_(03).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/21/Villa_of_the_former_Radio_Tirana_%2803%29.jpg/220px-Villa_of_the_former_Radio_Tirana_%2803%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="125" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/21/Villa_of_the_former_Radio_Tirana_%2803%29.jpg/330px-Villa_of_the_former_Radio_Tirana_%2803%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/21/Villa_of_the_former_Radio_Tirana_%2803%29.jpg/440px-Villa_of_the_former_Radio_Tirana_%2803%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="5604" data-file-height="3172" /></a><figcaption>The former grounds of the headquarters of <a href="/wiki/Radio_Tirana" class="mw-redirect" title="Radio Tirana">Radio Tirana</a> in the capital of <a href="/wiki/Tirana" title="Tirana">Tirana</a>. <a href="/wiki/Radio_Televizioni_Shqiptar" class="mw-redirect" title="Radio Televizioni Shqiptar">Radio Televizioni Shqiptar</a> (RTSH) was initially inaugurated as Radio Tirana in 1938 prior to the <a href="/wiki/World_War_II" title="World War II">World War II</a>.</figcaption></figure>
<p>The <a href="/wiki/Freedom_of_press" class="mw-redirect" title="Freedom of press">freedom of press</a> and <a href="/wiki/Freedom_of_speech" title="Freedom of speech">speech</a>, and the right to free expression is guaranteed in the <a href="/wiki/Constitution_of_Albania" title="Constitution of Albania">constitution of Albania</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-350" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-350">&#91;348&#93;</a></sup> Albania was ranked 84th on the <a href="/wiki/Press_Freedom_Index" class="mw-redirect" title="Press Freedom Index">Press Freedom Index</a> of 2020 compiled by the <a href="/wiki/Reporters_Without_Borders" title="Reporters Without Borders">Reporters Without Borders</a>, with its score steadily declining since 2003.<sup id="cite_ref-351" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-351">&#91;349&#93;</a></sup> Nevertheless, in the 2020 report of <a href="/wiki/Freedom_in_the_World" title="Freedom in the World">Freedom in the World</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Freedom_House" title="Freedom House">Freedom House</a> classified the freedoms of press and speech in Albania as partly free from political interference and manipulation.<sup id="cite_ref-352" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-352">&#91;350&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p><a href="/wiki/Radio_Televizioni_Shqiptar" class="mw-redirect" title="Radio Televizioni Shqiptar">Radio Televizioni Shqiptar</a> (RTSH) is the <a href="/wiki/National_broadcaster" class="mw-redirect" title="National broadcaster">national broadcaster</a> corporation of Albania operating numerous television and radio stations in the country.<sup id="cite_ref-353" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-353">&#91;351&#93;</a></sup> The three major private broadcaster corporations are <a href="/wiki/Top_Channel" title="Top Channel">Top Channel</a>, <a href="/wiki/TV_Klan" class="mw-redirect" title="TV Klan">Televizioni Klan</a> and <a href="/wiki/Vizion_Plus" title="Vizion Plus">Vizion Plus</a> whose content are distributed throughout Albania and beyond its territory in <a href="/wiki/Kosovo" title="Kosovo">Kosovo</a> and other <a href="/wiki/Albanian_language" title="Albanian language">Albanian-speaking</a> territories.<sup id="cite_ref-cia_fb2020_283-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-cia_fb2020-283">&#91;281&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Albanian cinema has its roots in the 20th century and developed after the country's <a href="/wiki/Albanian_Declaration_of_Independence" title="Albanian Declaration of Independence">declaration of independence</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Cinema_354-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Cinema-354">&#91;352&#93;</a></sup> The first <a href="/wiki/Movie_theater" title="Movie theater">movie theater</a> exclusively devoted to showing <a href="/wiki/Motion_pictures" class="mw-redirect" title="Motion pictures">motion pictures</a> was built in 1912 in <a href="/wiki/Shkod%C3%ABr" title="Shkodër">Shkodër</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Cinema_354-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Cinema-354">&#91;352&#93;</a></sup> During the <a href="/wiki/Peoples_Republic_of_Albania" class="mw-redirect" title="Peoples Republic of Albania">Peoples Republic of Albania</a>, Albanian cinema developed rapidly with the inauguration of the <a href="/wiki/Kinostudio_Shqip%C3%ABria_e_Re" class="mw-redirect" title="Kinostudio Shqipëria e Re">Kinostudio Shqipëria e Re</a> in Tirana.<sup id="cite_ref-Cinema_354-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Cinema-354">&#91;352&#93;</a></sup> In 1953, the Albanian-Soviet <a href="/wiki/Epic_film" title="Epic film">epic film</a>, the <a href="/wiki/The_Great_Warrior_Skanderbeg" title="The Great Warrior Skanderbeg">Great Warrior Skanderbeg</a>, was released chronicling the life and fight of the medieval Albanian hero <a href="/wiki/Gjergj_Kastriot_Skanderbeg" class="mw-redirect" title="Gjergj Kastriot Skanderbeg">Skanderbeg</a>. It went on to win the international prize at the <a href="/wiki/1954_Cannes_Film_Festival" title="1954 Cannes Film Festival">1954 Cannes Film Festival</a>. In 2003, the <a href="/wiki/Tirana_International_Film_Festival" title="Tirana International Film Festival">Tirana International Film Festival</a> was established, the largest film festival in the country. The <a href="/wiki/Durr%C3%ABs_Amphitheatre" class="mw-redirect" title="Durrës Amphitheatre">Durrës Amphitheatre</a> is host to the <a href="/wiki/Durr%C3%ABs_International_Film_Festival" class="mw-redirect" title="Durrës International Film Festival">Durrës International Film Festival</a>, the second largest film festival.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Music">Music</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Music_of_Albania" title="Music of Albania">Music of Albania</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:A_traditional_male_folk_group_from_Skrapar.JPG" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2a/A_traditional_male_folk_group_from_Skrapar.JPG/220px-A_traditional_male_folk_group_from_Skrapar.JPG" decoding="async" width="220" height="165" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2a/A_traditional_male_folk_group_from_Skrapar.JPG/330px-A_traditional_male_folk_group_from_Skrapar.JPG 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2a/A_traditional_male_folk_group_from_Skrapar.JPG/440px-A_traditional_male_folk_group_from_Skrapar.JPG 2x" data-file-width="2048" data-file-height="1536" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Albanian_iso-polyphony" class="mw-redirect" title="Albanian iso-polyphony">Albanian iso-polyphony</a> is designated as an <a href="/wiki/UNESCO" title="UNESCO">UNESCO</a> <a href="/wiki/Masterpieces_of_the_Oral_and_Intangible_Heritage_of_Humanity" title="Masterpieces of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity">Masterpiece of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-355" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-355">&#91;353&#93;</a></sup></figcaption></figure>
<p>Albanian folk music is a prominent part of the national identity, and continues to play a major part in overall <a href="/wiki/Music_of_Albania" title="Music of Albania">Albanian music</a>. Folk music can be divided into two stylistic groups, mainly the northern <a href="/wiki/Gheg_Albanian" title="Gheg Albanian">Gheg</a> varieties, and southern <a href="/wiki/Lab%C3%ABria" title="Labëria">Lab</a> and <a href="/wiki/Tosk_Albanian" title="Tosk Albanian">Tosk</a> varieties. Northern and southern traditions are contrasted by a rugged tone from the north, and the more relaxed southern form of music.
</p><p>Many songs concern events from <a href="/wiki/History_of_Albania" title="History of Albania">Albanian history</a> and <a href="/wiki/Culture_of_Albania" title="Culture of Albania">culture</a>, including traditional themes of honour, hospitality, treachery, and revenge. The first compilation of Albanian folk music was made by two <a href="/wiki/Himara" class="mw-redirect" title="Himara">Himariot</a> musicians, <a href="/wiki/Ne%C3%A7o_Muko" title="Neço Muko">Neço Muka</a> and Koço Çakali, in Paris, during their work with Albanian soprano <a href="/wiki/Tefta_Tashko-Ko%C3%A7o" title="Tefta Tashko-Koço">Tefta Tashko-Koço</a>. Several <a href="/wiki/Phonograph_record" title="Phonograph record">gramophone</a> compilations were recorded at the time by the three artists, which eventually led to the recognition of <a href="/wiki/Albanian_iso-polyphony" class="mw-redirect" title="Albanian iso-polyphony">Albanian iso-polyphony</a> as a <a href="/wiki/UNESCO" title="UNESCO">UNESCO</a> <a href="/wiki/UNESCO_Intangible_Cultural_Heritage_Lists" title="UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage Lists">Intangible Cultural Heritage</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-356" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-356">&#91;354&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p><a href="/wiki/Festivali_i_K%C3%ABng%C3%ABs" title="Festivali i Këngës">Festivali i Këngës</a> is a traditional Albanian song contest organised by the national broadcaster <a href="/wiki/Radio_Televizioni_Shqiptar" class="mw-redirect" title="Radio Televizioni Shqiptar">Radio Televizioni Shqiptar</a> (RTSH). The festival is celebrated annually since its inauguration in 1962 and has launched the careers of some of Albania's most successful singers including <a href="/wiki/Va%C3%A7e_Zela" title="Vaçe Zela">Vaçe Zela</a> and <a href="/wiki/Parashqevi_Simaku" title="Parashqevi Simaku">Parashqevi Simaku</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-357" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-357">&#91;355&#93;</a></sup> It is significantly a music competition among Albanian performers presenting unreleased songs in premiere, composed by Albanian authors and voted by juries or by public.
</p><p>Contemporary artists <a href="/wiki/Rita_Ora" title="Rita Ora">Rita Ora</a>, <a href="/wiki/Bebe_Rexha" title="Bebe Rexha">Bebe Rexha</a>, <a href="/wiki/Era_Istrefi" title="Era Istrefi">Era Istrefi</a>, <a href="/wiki/Dua_Lipa" title="Dua Lipa">Dua Lipa</a>, <a href="/wiki/Ava_Max" title="Ava Max">Ava Max</a>, <a href="/wiki/Bleona" title="Bleona">Bleona</a>, <a href="/wiki/Elvana_Gjata" title="Elvana Gjata">Elvana Gjata</a>, <a href="/wiki/Ermonela_Jaho" title="Ermonela Jaho">Ermonela Jaho</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Inva_Mula" title="Inva Mula">Inva Mula</a> have achieved international recognition for their music,<sup id="cite_ref-358" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-358">&#91;356&#93;</a></sup> while soprano <a href="/wiki/Ermonela_Jaho" title="Ermonela Jaho">Ermonela Jaho</a> has been described by some as the "world's most acclaimed soprano".<sup id="cite_ref-359" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-359">&#91;357&#93;</a></sup> Albanian opera singer <a href="/wiki/Saimir_Pirgu" title="Saimir Pirgu">Saimir Pirgu</a> was nominated for the 2017 <a href="/wiki/Grammy_Award" class="mw-redirect" title="Grammy Award">Grammy Award</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-360" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-360">&#91;358&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Traditional_clothing">Traditional clothing</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Traditional_Albanian_clothing" class="mw-redirect" title="Traditional Albanian clothing">Traditional Albanian clothing</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Les_Danseurs_Albanais_by_Alexandre-Gabriel_Decamps_(c._1835).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/89/Les_Danseurs_Albanais_by_Alexandre-Gabriel_Decamps_%28c._1835%29.jpg/220px-Les_Danseurs_Albanais_by_Alexandre-Gabriel_Decamps_%28c._1835%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="137" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/89/Les_Danseurs_Albanais_by_Alexandre-Gabriel_Decamps_%28c._1835%29.jpg/330px-Les_Danseurs_Albanais_by_Alexandre-Gabriel_Decamps_%28c._1835%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/89/Les_Danseurs_Albanais_by_Alexandre-Gabriel_Decamps_%28c._1835%29.jpg/440px-Les_Danseurs_Albanais_by_Alexandre-Gabriel_Decamps_%28c._1835%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="771" data-file-height="481" /></a><figcaption><i>The Albanian Dancer</i> (1835) by French artist <a href="/wiki/Alexandre-Gabriel_Decamps" title="Alexandre-Gabriel Decamps">Alexandre-Gabriel Decamps</a>; the dancers are depicted wearing the <a href="/wiki/Fustanella" title="Fustanella">fustanella</a>, the <a href="/wiki/National_costume_of_Albania" class="mw-redirect" title="National costume of Albania">national costume of Albania</a>.</figcaption></figure>
<p>Every cultural and geographical region of Albania has its own specific variety of costume that vary in style, material, colour, shape, detail, and form.<sup id="cite_ref-361" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-361">&#91;359&#93;</a></sup> Presently, <a href="/wiki/National_costume_of_Albania" class="mw-redirect" title="National costume of Albania">national costumes</a> are most often worn during special events and celebrations, mostly at ethnic festivals, religious holidays, weddings, and by performing dance groups. Some elderly people continue to wear traditional clothing in their daily lives. Clothing was traditionally made mainly from local materials such as leather, wool, linen, hemp fibre, and silk; Albanian textiles are still embroidered in elaborate ancient patterns.
</p>
<div style="clear:both;"></div>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Literature">Literature</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1097763485"><table class="box-More_citations_needed_section plainlinks metadata ambox ambox-content ambox-Refimprove" role="presentation"><tbody><tr><td class="mbox-image"><div class="mbox-image-div"><span typeof="mw:File"><a href="/wiki/File:Question_book-new.svg" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/9/99/Question_book-new.svg/50px-Question_book-new.svg.png" decoding="async" width="50" height="39" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/9/99/Question_book-new.svg/75px-Question_book-new.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/9/99/Question_book-new.svg/100px-Question_book-new.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="512" data-file-height="399" /></a></span></div></td><td class="mbox-text"><div class="mbox-text-span">This section <b>needs additional citations for <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability" title="Wikipedia:Verifiability">verification</a></b>.<span class="hide-when-compact"> Please help <a href="/wiki/Special:EditPage/Albania" title="Special:EditPage/Albania">improve this article</a> by <a href="/wiki/Help:Referencing_for_beginners" title="Help:Referencing for beginners">adding citations to reliable sources</a>&#32;in this section. Unsourced material may be challenged and removed.</span>  <span class="date-container"><i>(<span class="date">October 2018</span>)</i></span><span class="hide-when-compact"><i> (<small><a href="/wiki/Help:Maintenance_template_removal" title="Help:Maintenance template removal">Learn how and when to remove this template message</a></small>)</i></span></div></td></tr></tbody></table>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Albanian_literature" title="Albanian literature">Albanian literature</a></div><figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Meshari.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/23/Meshari.jpg/220px-Meshari.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="149" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/23/Meshari.jpg/330px-Meshari.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/2/23/Meshari.jpg 2x" data-file-width="400" data-file-height="271" /></a><figcaption>An excerpt from the <a href="/wiki/Meshari" title="Meshari">Meshari</a> <i>(The Missal)</i> written by <a href="/wiki/Gjon_Buzuku" title="Gjon Buzuku">Gjon Buzuku</a> <small>(1555)</small></figcaption></figure>
<p>The cultural renaissance was first of all expressed through the development of the <a href="/wiki/Albanian_language" title="Albanian language">Albanian language</a> in the area of church texts and publications. The Protestant reforms invigorated hopes for the development of the local language and literary tradition, when cleric <a href="/wiki/Gjon_Buzuku" title="Gjon Buzuku">Gjon Buzuku</a> translated the <a href="/wiki/Catholic_liturgy" title="Catholic liturgy">Catholic liturgy</a> into Albanian, trying to do for Albanian what <a href="/wiki/Martin_Luther" title="Martin Luther">Martin Luther</a> had done for German. <a href="/wiki/Meshari" title="Meshari">Meshari</a> (<i>The Missal</i>) written by <a href="/wiki/Gjon_Buzuku" title="Gjon Buzuku">Gjon Buzuku</a> was published in 1555 and is considered one of the first literary work of written Albanian during the Middle Ages. The refined level of the language and the stabilised orthography must be the result of an earlier tradition of written Albanian, a tradition that is not well understood. However, there is some fragmented evidence, pre-dating Buzuku, which indicates that Albanian was written from at least the 14th century.
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Parashqevi_Qiriazi.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/68/Parashqevi_Qiriazi.jpg/170px-Parashqevi_Qiriazi.jpg" decoding="async" width="170" height="209" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/68/Parashqevi_Qiriazi.jpg/255px-Parashqevi_Qiriazi.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/68/Parashqevi_Qiriazi.jpg/340px-Parashqevi_Qiriazi.jpg 2x" data-file-width="598" data-file-height="734" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Parashqevi_Qiriazi" title="Parashqevi Qiriazi">Parashqevi Qiriazi</a> – teacher and feminist (1880–1970)</figcaption></figure>
<p>Albanian writings from these centuries must not have been religious texts only, but historical chronicles too. They are mentioned by the humanist <a href="/wiki/Marin_Barleti" title="Marin Barleti">Marin Barleti</a>, who in his book <a href="/wiki/Siege_of_Shkodra_(1478)#The_Book" class="mw-redirect" title="Siege of Shkodra (1478)">Siege of Shkodër</a> (<i>Rrethimi i Shkodrës</i>) from 1504, confirms that he leafed through such chronicles written in the language of the people (<i>in vernacula lingua</i>) as well as his famous biography of <a href="/wiki/Skanderbeg" title="Skanderbeg">Skanderbeg</a> <a href="/wiki/Marin_Barleti" title="Marin Barleti">Historia de vita et gestis Scanderbegi Epirotarum principis</a> (<i>History of Skanderbeg</i>) from 1508. The <i>History of Skanderbeg</i> is still the foundation of Skanderbeg studies and is considered an Albanian cultural treasure, vital to the formation of Albanian national self-consciousness.
</p><p>During the 16th and the 17th centuries, the <a href="/wiki/Catechism" title="Catechism">catechism</a> (<i>E mbësuame krishterë</i>) (Christian Teachings) from 1592 written by <a href="/wiki/Lek%C3%AB_Matr%C3%ABnga" class="mw-redirect" title="Lekë Matrënga">Lekë Matrënga</a>, (<i>Doktrina e krishterë</i>) (The Christian Doctrine) from 1618 and (<i>Rituale romanum</i>) 1621 by <a href="/wiki/Pjet%C3%ABr_Budi" title="Pjetër Budi">Pjetër Budi</a>, the first writer of original Albanian <a href="/wiki/Prose" title="Prose">prose</a> and poetry, an <a href="/wiki/Remorse" title="Remorse">apology</a> for George Castriot (1636) by <a href="/wiki/Frang_Bardhi" title="Frang Bardhi">Frang Bardhi</a>, who also published a dictionary and <a href="/wiki/Folklore" title="Folklore">folklore</a> creations, the theological-philosophical treaty <i><a href="/wiki/Cuneus_Prophetarum" title="Cuneus Prophetarum">Cuneus Prophetarum</a></i> (The Band of Prophets) (1685) by <a href="/wiki/Pjet%C3%ABr_Bogdani" title="Pjetër Bogdani">Pjetër Bogdani</a>, the most universal personality of Albanian <a href="/wiki/Middle_Ages" title="Middle Ages">Middle Ages</a>, were published in <a href="/wiki/Albanian_language" title="Albanian language">Albanian</a>. The most famous Albanian writer in the 20th and 21st century is probably <a href="/wiki/Ismail_Kadare" title="Ismail Kadare">Ismail Kadare</a>.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Sports">Sports</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/Albania_at_the_Olympics" title="Albania at the Olympics">Albania at the Olympics</a> and <a href="/wiki/Albania_at_the_Mediterranean_Games" title="Albania at the Mediterranean Games">Albania at the Mediterranean Games</a></div>
<p>Albania participated at the <a href="/wiki/1972_Summer_Olympics" title="1972 Summer Olympics">Olympic Games in 1972</a> for the first time. The country made their Winter Olympic Games debut in <a href="/wiki/Winter_Olympics_2006" class="mw-redirect" title="Winter Olympics 2006">2006</a>. Albania missed the next four games, two of them due to the 1980 and 1984 boycotts, but returned for the 1992 games in <a href="/wiki/1992_Olympic_Winter_Games" class="mw-redirect" title="1992 Olympic Winter Games">Barcelona</a>. Since then, Albania have participated in all games. Albania normally competes in events that include swimming, athletics, weightlifting, shooting and wrestling. The country have been represented by the <a href="/wiki/National_Olympic_Committee_of_Albania" class="mw-redirect" title="National Olympic Committee of Albania">National Olympic Committee of Albania</a> since 1972. The nation has participated at the <a href="/wiki/Mediterranean_Games" title="Mediterranean Games">Mediterranean Games</a> since the games of <a href="/wiki/1987_Mediterranean_Games" title="1987 Mediterranean Games">1987</a> in Syria. The Albanian athletes have won a total of 43 (8 gold, 17 silver and 18 bronze) medals from <a href="/wiki/1987_Mediterranean_Games" title="1987 Mediterranean Games">1987</a> to <a href="/wiki/2013_Mediterranean_Games" title="2013 Mediterranean Games">2013</a>.
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Muzeu_Arkeologjike_Tirane.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8b/Muzeu_Arkeologjike_Tirane.jpg/220px-Muzeu_Arkeologjike_Tirane.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="165" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8b/Muzeu_Arkeologjike_Tirane.jpg/330px-Muzeu_Arkeologjike_Tirane.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8b/Muzeu_Arkeologjike_Tirane.jpg/440px-Muzeu_Arkeologjike_Tirane.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1280" data-file-height="960" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Arena_Komb%C3%ABtare" title="Arena Kombëtare">Arena Kombëtare</a> in central Tirana</figcaption></figure>
<p>Popular sports in Albania include <a href="/wiki/Football_in_Albania" title="Football in Albania">football</a>, weightlifting, <a href="/wiki/Albania_national_basketball_team" class="mw-redirect" title="Albania national basketball team">basketball</a>, volleyball, tennis, swimming, <a href="/wiki/Rugby_union" title="Rugby union">rugby union</a> and gymnastics. Football is by far the most popular sport in Albania. It is governed by the <a href="/wiki/Football_Association_of_Albania" class="mw-redirect" title="Football Association of Albania">Football Association of Albania</a> (<a href="/wiki/Albanian_language" title="Albanian language">Albanian</a>: <i lang="sq">Federata Shqiptare e Futbollit</i>, F.SH.F.), which has membership in <a href="/wiki/FIFA" title="FIFA">FIFA</a> and <a href="/wiki/UEFA" title="UEFA">UEFA</a>.
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/Albania_national_football_team" title="Albania national football team">Albania national football team</a>, ranking 51st in the <a href="/wiki/FIFA_World_Rankings" class="mw-redirect" title="FIFA World Rankings">World</a> in 2017 (highest 22nd on 22 August 2015) have won the <a href="/wiki/1946_Balkan_Cup" title="1946 Balkan Cup">1946 Balkan Cup</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Rothmans_International_Tournament_2000" class="mw-redirect" title="Rothmans International Tournament 2000">Malta Rothmans International Tournament 2000</a>, but had never participated in any major <a href="/wiki/UEFA" title="UEFA">UEFA</a> or <a href="/wiki/FIFA" title="FIFA">FIFA</a> tournament, until <a href="/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2016" title="UEFA Euro 2016">UEFA Euro 2016</a>, Albania's first ever appearance at the continental tournament and at a major men's football tournament. Albania scored their first ever goal in a major tournament and secured their first ever win in European Championship when they beat <a href="/wiki/Romania_national_football_team" title="Romania national football team">Romania</a> by 1–0 in a <a href="/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2016" title="UEFA Euro 2016">UEFA Euro 2016</a> match on 19 June 2016.<sup id="cite_ref-362" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-362">&#91;360&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-363" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-363">&#91;361&#93;</a></sup> The most successful football clubs are <a href="/wiki/KF_Sk%C3%ABnderbeu_Kor%C3%A7%C3%AB" title="KF Skënderbeu Korçë">Skënderbeu</a>, <a href="/wiki/KF_Tirana" title="KF Tirana">KF Tirana</a>, <a href="/wiki/FK_Dinamo_Tirana" class="mw-redirect" title="FK Dinamo Tirana">Dinamo Tirana</a>, <a href="/wiki/FK_Partizani_Tirana" title="FK Partizani Tirana">Partizani</a> and <a href="/wiki/KF_Vllaznia_Shkod%C3%ABr" title="KF Vllaznia Shkodër">Vllaznia</a>.
</p><p>Weightlifting is one of the most successful individual sport for the Albanians, with the national team winning medals at the <a href="/wiki/European_Weightlifting_Championships" title="European Weightlifting Championships">European Weightlifting Championships</a> and the rest international competitions. Albanian weightlifters have won a total of 16 medals at the <a href="/wiki/European_Weightlifting_Championships" title="European Weightlifting Championships">European Championships</a> with 1 of them being gold, 7 silver and 8 bronze. In the <a href="/wiki/World_Weightlifting_Championships" title="World Weightlifting Championships">World Weightlifting Championships</a>, the Albanian weightlifting team has won in <a href="/wiki/1972_World_Weightlifting_Championships" title="1972 World Weightlifting Championships">1972</a> a gold in <a href="/wiki/2002_World_Weightlifting_Championships" title="2002 World Weightlifting Championships">2002</a> a silver and in <a href="/wiki/2011_World_Weightlifting_Championships" title="2011 World Weightlifting Championships">2011</a> a bronze medal.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Diaspora">Diaspora</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main pages: <a href="/wiki/Albanian_diaspora" title="Albanian diaspora">Albanian diaspora</a> and <a href="/wiki/Category:Albanian_diaspora" title="Category:Albanian diaspora">Albanian communities</a></div>
<p>Historically, the Albanian people have established several communities in many regions throughout Southern Europe. The <a href="/wiki/Albanian_diaspora" title="Albanian diaspora">Albanian diaspora</a> has been formed since the late <a href="/wiki/Middle_Ages" title="Middle Ages">Middle Ages</a>, when they emigrated to places such as Italy, especially in <a href="/wiki/Sicily" title="Sicily">Sicily</a> and <a href="/wiki/Calabria" title="Calabria">Calabria</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Greece" title="Greece">Greece</a> to escape either various socio-political difficulties or the <a href="/wiki/Ottoman_Empire" title="Ottoman Empire">Ottoman conquest</a> of Albania.<sup id="cite_ref-364" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-364">&#91;362&#93;</a></sup> Following the <a href="/wiki/Fall_of_communism_in_Albania" title="Fall of communism in Albania">fall of communism</a>, large numbers of Albanians have migrated to countries such as Australia, Canada, France, Germany, <a href="/wiki/Greece" title="Greece">Greece</a>, Italy, <a href="/wiki/Scandinavia" title="Scandinavia">Scandinavia</a>, <a href="/wiki/Switzerland" title="Switzerland">Switzerland</a>, the United Kingdom and the United States. Albanian <a href="/wiki/Minority_group" title="Minority group">minorities</a> are present in the neighbouring territories such as the west of <a href="/wiki/North_Macedonia" title="North Macedonia">North Macedonia</a>, the east of <a href="/wiki/Montenegro" title="Montenegro">Montenegro</a>, <a href="/wiki/Kosovo" title="Kosovo">Kosovo</a> in its entirety and southern <a href="/wiki/Serbia" title="Serbia">Serbia</a>. In <a href="/wiki/Kosovo" title="Kosovo">Kosovo</a>, Albanians are the largest ethnic group in the country. Altogether, the number of ethnic Albanians living abroad is estimated to be higher than the total population inside Albania.
</p>

UNESCO. pp.&#160;UNESCO. <q>Situated on the shores of Lake Ohrid, the town of Ohrid is one of the oldest human settlements in Europe; Lake Ohrid is a superlative natural phenomenon, providing refuge for numerous endemic and relict freshwater species of flora and fauna dating from the tertiary period.
